column5: Fog lines the stairs leading up to The Triumvirate's chambers.{w}\nI was confident a moment ago, but this sight fills me with unease.{w}\nI've never seen anything like it, and it's very concerning to me.
column6: 浓雾弥漫在通往三人执政团议事厅的阶梯上。{w}\n方才我还满怀信心，可这景象却让我心神不宁。{w}\n我从未见过这样的东西，这让我深感忧虑。

column5: I couldn't see off the edges of the stairs, and there was no railing.{w}\nThe slightest stumble could send me back down to the atrium.{w}\nI do need to go back there. But — that's not the way I'd do it.
column6: 我看不清阶梯的边缘，也没有任何护栏。{w}\n稍有失足，我就会一路摔回中庭。{w}\n我确实得回去一趟。但——绝不是以这种方式。

column5: I have one piece of advice for you, [firstname].\nDon't let them talk to you. Just kill them, with no question.\nAll they'll do is try to justify their actions, and earn your sympathy.
column6: 我有一句忠告给你，[firstname]。\n别让他们开口跟你说话。什么都别问，直接杀了他们。\n他们只会试图为自己的所作所为辩解，好博取你的同情。

column5: They prey on the minds of the weak. Of those that they can mould.\nI know you're strong, but they just have this way of convincing you.\nI'd hate to see that happen to you. So remember. Kill them all.
column6: 他们专挑心智软弱、能被他们塑造的人下手。\n我知道你很坚强，可他们就是有办法说服你。\n我不愿看到你变成那样。所以记住，把他们全部杀掉。

column5: I tell him that I don't care what they say to me. I'm here to kill them.{w}\nThey could speak to me all they wished. They'd accomplish nothing.{w}\nAn easy goal to have in mind. But in practice — I guess I had no idea.
column6: 我告诉他，我不在乎他们对我说什么。我来这里就是为了杀他们。{w}\n他们尽可以对我畅所欲言，也改变不了什么。{w}\n这话说着容易。可真正面对时——我想我根本没有料到。

column5: I'd have to find out however. Someone steps out of the room ahead of us.{w}\nAs they move toward us, I can see the white and gold of their cloak.{w}\nOne of them left their chambers...? I thought they didn't do that.
column6: 可我终究得弄清楚。这时，有人从我们前方的房间里走了出来。{w}\n当他们朝我们走来时，我看清了那件白金相间的斗篷。{w}\n他们中的一人离开了议事厅……？我还以为他们从不这样做。

column5: Sovy — you've returned.\nWere we not clear enough...?\nA permanent exile is non-negotiable.
column6: 索维——你回来了。\n难道我们说得还不够清楚吗……？\n永久流放，没有商量的余地。

column5: But you said—!
column6: 可你明明说过——！

column5: He turns to them, and motions as if he's pleading.
column6: 他转身面向他们，比划着，像是在哀求。

column5: You said I could come back if I brought the blade!\nIs this not what you wanted? Was it not a test...?
column6: 你说过，只要我带回那把剑，我就能回来！\n这不正是你想要的吗？难道这不是一场考验吗……？

column5: The Triumvir looks down at both of us, and sighs.
column6: 执政官俯视着我们两人，叹了口气。

column5: You think that you can fool us so easily?\nWe know where your allegiance lies, Sovy.\nThere is nothing in this world we cannot see.
column6: 你以为能这么轻易骗过我们吗？\n我们知道你忠于谁，索维。\n这世上没有任何东西能逃过我们的眼睛。

column5: Sovy gritted his teeth. I could tell that he was angry.{w}\nI'm confused, but I trust him. I knew he was on my side.{w}\nAt least, that's what I thought. Everything changes in an instant.
column6: 索维咬紧了牙关。我能看出他动了怒。{w}\n我很困惑，但我信任他。我知道他站在我这边。{w}\n至少，我是这么以为的。而一切都在瞬间改变了。

column5: Everything I did, I did for you...!\nWere you really too foolish to realize that!?\nMy attempt to help The Rebellion was only an act!
column6: 我所做的一切，都是为了你们……！\n你们真的蠢到看不出来吗！？\n我帮助反抗军，不过是在演戏！

column5: What..?
column6: 什么……？

column5: I've brought the enemy, and the blade, to your doorstep.\nEven after this, you deny me my redemption!?
column6: 我把敌人和那把剑都送到了你们门前。\n即便如此，你们还是不肯给我赎罪的机会吗！？

column5: I immediately try to run, but Sovy grabs my right arm.{w}\nAs much as I struggle, it's no use. He's too strong.{w}\nI'm filled with fright. How could he do this...!?
column6: 我立刻想逃，可索维抓住了我的右臂。{w}\n无论我怎么挣扎都无济于事。他太强了。{w}\n我满心恐惧。他怎么能做出这种事……！？

column5: I immediately try to run, but Sovy grabs my left arm.{w}\nAs much as I struggle, it's no use. He's too strong.{w}\nI'm filled with fright. How could he do this...!?
column6: 我立刻想逃，可索维抓住了我的左臂。{w}\n无论我怎么挣扎都无济于事。他太强了。{w}\n我满心恐惧。他怎么能做出这种事……！？

column5: You've done nothing but bring an armed enemy into our home.\nYour judgment is clouded, Sovy. We decline your offer.
column6: 你所做的不过是把一名全副武装的敌人带进了我们的家。\n你的判断被蒙蔽了，索维。我们拒绝你的提议。

column5: A second after, Sovy phases the blade into his hands.{w}\nThen, much to my regret, he slices through my arm with ease.{w}\nI scream, and then from the elbow down, almost nothing remains.
column6: 一秒之后，索维将剑实体化到手中。{w}\n紧接着，令我悔恨不已的是，他轻而易举地斩断了我的手臂。{w}\n我放声尖叫，而从手肘往下，几乎什么也没剩下。

column5: Then take {i}this{/i} as an offering...!\nThat arm will never again be used against you.\nBefore all of us, [firstname] is defenseless.
column6: 那就把{i}这个{/i}当作献礼吧……！\n那条手臂再也不可能被用来对付你们了。\n在我们所有人面前，[firstname]已毫无防备。

column5: I don't feel anything, almost as if my body numbs itself from the trauma.{w}\nBut the sight is all too real. My lower arm, limp, and dead on the floor.{w}\nBlood spurts from the wound, and I look at Sovy in disbelief.
column6: 我什么都感觉不到，仿佛身体因创伤而麻木了。{w}\n可眼前的景象却无比真实。我的小臂软弱无力地瘫死在地上。{w}\n鲜血从伤口喷涌而出，我难以置信地看向索维。

column5: He makes direct eye contact with me, and then looks at the torch.{w}\nI'm still gripping it tightly, and that's when things make sense.{w}\nWas he trying to fool them? I still have use of my good arm.
column6: 他直视着我的眼睛，随后看向那支火把。{w}\n我仍旧紧紧握着它，就在那时，我明白了一切。{w}\n他是在骗他们吗？我那条完好的手臂还能用。

column5: I slump against the wall, and use the torch to burn the wound shut.{w}\nA disgusting smell fills the air, and I can hear cracking and sizzling.{w}\nThis is all I can do, while I watch Sovy ascend the stairs with the blade.
column6: 我瘫靠在墙上，用火把将伤口烧灼封住。{w}\n一股恶臭弥漫在空气中，我能听见噼啪的灼烧声。{w}\n眼看着索维带着那把剑登上阶梯，我能做的也只有这些了。

column5: You continue to surprise us, Sovy.\nVery well. Let us talk.
column6: 你总是让我们意外，索维。\n好吧。那我们就谈谈。

column5: The Triumvir looks down at my scabbard.{w}\nThey definitely believe Sovy removed my dominant arm.{w}\nI don't know why any of this is happening, but I let it all unfold.
column6: 执政官低头看了看我的剑鞘。{w}\n他们显然相信索维斩断的是我的惯用手臂。{w}\n我不知道这一切为何会发生，但我任由它发展下去。

column5: I trust him.
column6: 我相信他。

column5: Thank you, Master.\nI am sorry for letting you down in the past.\nI can only hope that this offering is enough to please you.
column6: 谢谢您，主人。\n过去让您失望了，我很抱歉。\n我只希望这份献礼足以让您满意。

column5: He continues to walk up the stairs, slowly, as if somewhat scared.{w}\nIf I were him, I wouldn't want to make any sudden movements, either.{w}\nThe Triumvirate has the advantage here. All we could do was try our best.
column6: 他继续缓缓走上阶梯，仿佛有些害怕。{w}\n如果我是他，我也不会想做出任何突然的动作。{w}\n在这里，占上风的是三人执政团。我们能做的只有尽力而为。

column5: Remove threats, to ensure the continued reign of Alestia's leaders.\nIs that not what you wanted..? Is that not the role of The Grand Inquisitor?
column6: 清除威胁，以确保阿莱斯蒂亚的统治者能长久掌权。\n这不正是您想要的吗……？这不正是大审判官的职责吗？

column5: As he speaks, he reaches the top of the stairs, and faces his Master.{w}\nThe Triumvir lets out another loud sigh, and proceeds to nod a few times.{w}\nBy now, I'm almost coherent again, and the wound bleeds no more. Burnt shut.
column6: 他说着，走到了阶梯顶端，面对着他的主人。{w}\n执政官又重重叹了口气，接着点了几下头。{w}\n此时，我几乎恢复了清醒，伤口也不再流血了。已经被灼烧封住。

column5: You are right. Kneel, Sovy, and pledge your loyalty.\nThen, turn that blade on The Monarch, and take his soul.\nThat's all we need. The blade, and the power inside him.
column6: 你说得对。跪下吧，索维，宣誓效忠。\n然后，把那把剑转向君主，取走他的灵魂。\n我们要的就这些。那把剑，以及他体内的力量。

column5: You are right. Kneel, Sovy, and pledge your loyalty.\nThen, turn that blade on The Monarch, and take her soul.\nThat's all we need. The blade, and the power inside her.
column6: 你说得对。跪下吧，索维，宣誓效忠。\n然后，把那把剑转向君主，取走她的灵魂。\n我们要的就这些。那把剑，以及她体内的力量。

column5: Sovy immediately drops the blade to his side, and kneels down.{w}\nIt hits the ground with a loud metallic clang, then rests there, motionless.
column6: 索维立刻将剑垂到身侧，跪了下来。{w}\n剑落在地上，发出一声铿锵的金属巨响，随后静止不动地躺在那儿。

column5: Yes, whatever you say. I will continue to serve.\nAs The Grand Inquisitor, I have only one goal.\nRemoving threats to the throne of Alestia.
column6: 是，一切都听您的。我会继续效力。\n作为大审判官，我只有一个目标。\n清除对阿莱斯蒂亚王座的威胁。

column5: He trembles, frightened, as The Triumvir nods.
column6: 执政官点了点头，他则害怕地颤抖着。

column5: And I shall start with you...
column6: 那么，就从你们开始吧……

column5: A moment later, the blade disappears from the ground.{w}\nBut it doesn't return to Sovy's hands, or even mine.{w}\nIt phases directly through the chest of The Triumvir.
column6: 片刻之后，地上的剑消失了。{w}\n但它没有回到索维手中，也没有回到我的手中。{w}\n它径直穿过了那位执政官的胸膛。

column5: S-Sovy...!?
He rises to his feet, and grips the handle of the blade.{w}\nI can see tears streaming from his eyes. Sad at what he's done.{w}\nHe's shaking, as if he almost refuses to believe that this is real.
column6: 他站起身来，握住剑柄。{w}\n我能看见泪水从他眼中涌出。他是为自己的所作所为而悲伤。{w}\n他浑身发抖，仿佛几乎不愿相信这是真的。

column5: I hate that you're making me do this...\nI hate the man that you've made me become...
column6: 我恨你们逼我做出这种事……\n我恨你们把我变成了这样的人……

column5: S-Sovy...
column6: 索、索维……

column5: And a moment later, he pulls out the blade.{w}\nThen, with a harsh kick, The Triumvir flies off the edge.{w}\nI can hear them scream as they fall, and then, the screams fade.
column6: 片刻之后，他拔出了剑。{w}\n接着，一脚狠狠踢出，那位执政官飞出了阶梯边缘。{w}\n我能听见他们坠落时的惨叫，随后，那叫声渐渐消散。

column5: Sovy drops the blade, and then drops back down to his knees.{w}\nI start walking up the stairs, shocked at what I just saw.{w}\nOne of them was dead...? Now, only two more remain.
column6: 索维丢下剑，又颓然跪倒在地。{w}\n我震惊于方才所见，开始向阶梯上走去。{w}\n他们中的一个死了……？现在，只剩下两个了。

column5: [firstname]...\nTake the blade and go.\nEnd this foolish war. Please...
column6: [firstname]……\n带上那把剑，走吧。\n终结这场愚蠢的战争。求你了……

column5: I summon the blade back into my hand, and walk up the stairs.{w}\nI stop, as I arrive beside him. But he simply shakes his head.{w}\nI consider placing my hand on his shoulder, but it's no use.
column6: 我将剑召回手中，走上阶梯。{w}\n走到他身边时，我停下脚步。可他只是摇了摇头。{w}\n我想把手搭在他肩上，却毫无意义。

column5: Just go...
column6: 走吧……

column5: With a sigh of regret, I realize that there's nothing I can do.{w}\nI wouldn't even have time to chastise him. I decide to enter their chambers.{w}\nHis cries fill my ears, and dissipate with each step I take toward the end.
column6: 我遗憾地叹了口气，意识到自己什么也做不了。{w}\n我甚至没有时间责备他。我决定走进他们的议事厅。{w}\n他的哭声灌满我的耳朵，随着我一步步走向终点而渐渐消散。

column5: Either the end of The Triumvirate, or the end of myself...
column6: 要么是三人执政团的终结，要么是我自己的终结……

column5: [firstname], I'm sorry...\nI think this is the end for me.\nHonestly, it {i}has{/i} been for a long time.
column6: [firstname]，对不起……\n我想这就是我的终点了。\n说实话，它{i}早就{/i}是了。

column5: I summon the blade back into my hand.{w}\nIt was clear that he needed some consolation.{w}\nBut, a second later, I realize I'd never get the chance.
column6: 我将剑召回手中。{w}\n他显然需要一些安慰。{w}\n可一秒之后，我意识到自己再也没有这个机会了。

column5: With tears in his eyes, he throws himself off the edge of the stairs.{w}\nI start to run up the stairs, but it's no use. It's far too late when I get to the top.{w}\nHe falls, but lets out no scream. He faces his end with courage, unlike his Master.
column6: 他眼含泪水，纵身跃出了阶梯边缘。{w}\n我拔腿向阶梯上奔去，却无济于事。等我赶到顶端时，早已太迟了。{w}\n他坠落了，却没有发出一声叫喊。他勇敢地面对了自己的结局，不像他的主人。

column5: There was nothing I could do. {w}\nI couldn't waste a second now that I was here.{w}\nMourning him, or crying, would only result in death.
column6: 我无能为力。{w}\n既然已经来到这里，我一秒也不能浪费。{w}\n为他哀悼，或是哭泣，只会招来死亡。

column5: I'm full of regret. How could I save the world, if I couldn't even save {i}him{/i}?{w}\nThat worry rises within me as I slowly enter The Triumvirate's chambers.{w}\nI have no idea what awaited me, but I knew that it would be the end.
column6: 我满心悔恨。如果连{i}他{/i}都救不了，我又怎么能拯救这个世界？{w}\n当我缓缓走进三人执政团的议事厅时，这份忧虑在心中升起。{w}\n我不知道前方等待我的是什么，但我知道，那将是终点。

column5: Either the end of The Triumvirate, or the end of myself...
column6: 要么是三人执政团的终结，要么是我自己的终结……

column5: The ringing of the bell echoes in my ears. It's almost deafening.{w}\nI'm relieved to know that Fortaime survived, and succeeded.{w}\nMe and Ulric stand in the darkness, and it's hard to see.
column6: 钟声在耳中回荡，几乎震耳欲聋。{w}\n得知福泰姆活了下来，并且成功了，我松了口气。{w}\n我和乌尔里克站在黑暗中，四周几乎什么都看不清。

column5: Here, you'll be needing this.
column6: 给，你会需要这个。

column5: He hands me a torch that was hung against the wall.
column6: 他把一支挂在墙上的火把递给我。

column5: And watch your step as we go up those stairs.\nIf you fall off the edge — well, you know how high we are.
column6: 上楼的时候小心脚下。\n要是从边缘摔下去——你也知道我们有多高。

column5: I nod. The thought filled me with fright.{w}\nI hold out the torch, and see the bizarre sight before me.{w}\nThe walls are lined with gears, just like those on the blade.
column6: 我点点头。这个念头让我不寒而栗。{w}\n我举起火把，看见了眼前那幅怪异的景象。{w}\n墙壁上排列着齿轮，就跟那把剑上的一模一样。

column5: They spin, and rotate in directions that they shouldn't.{w}\nIt makes no sense to me. But then again, neither does the blade.{w}\nThe gear on the base spun in a way that was impossible, too.
column6: 它们旋转着，朝着本不该转动的方向。{w}\n我完全无法理解。不过话说回来，那把剑也一样让我费解。{w}\n底座上的齿轮当初也是以不可能的方式转动的。

column5: Fog lines the stairs leading up to The Triumvirate's chambers.{w}\nI was confident a moment ago, but this sight fills me with unease.{w}\nI've never seen anything like it, and it's very concerning to me.

column6: 可我终究得弄清楚。这时，有人从我们前方的房间里走了出来。{w}\n当他们朝我们走来时，我看清了那件白金相间的斗篷。{w}\n他们中的一人离开了议事厅……？我还以为他们从不这样做。

column5: Ulric — this is quite a surprise.\nIt's been ages since we've seen your face.\nHave you come to grovel in the face of your defeat?
column6: 乌尔里克——真是意外。\n我们已经很久没见过你的脸了。\n你是来面对败局摇尾乞怜的吗？

column5: I've come here to end this war.\nI bring an offering. The blade, and [firstname].\nDo with him what you will, but I ask for your surrender.
column6: 我来此是为了终结这场战争。\n我带来了一份献礼。那把剑，还有[firstname]。\n你们想怎么处置他都行，但我请求你们投降。

column5: I've come here to end this war.\nI bring an offering. The blade, and [firstname].\nDo with her what you will, but I ask for your surrender.
column6: 我来此是为了终结这场战争。\n我带来了一份献礼。那把剑，还有[firstname]。\n你们想怎么处置她都行，但我请求你们投降。

column5: Leave this world, and never return.\nLive your lives in peace, somewhere far away.\nJust stay out or our business, and leave us alone.
column6: 离开这个世界，永远别再回来。\n去远方平静地生活吧。\n别再来干涉我们的事，让我们清静。

column5: What...!? Ulric was selling me out...!?{w}\nI turn and try to run, but he immediately grabs my right arm.{w}\nI'm filled with fright. I'm not strong enough to break free from his grip.
column6: 什么……！？乌尔里克把我出卖了……！？{w}\n我转身想逃，可他立刻抓住了我的右臂。{w}\n我满心恐惧，力气不足以挣脱他的钳制。

column5: What...!? Ulric was selling me out...!?{w}\nI turn and try to run, but he immediately grabs my left arm.{w}\nI'm filled with fright, but I'm not strong enough to break free from his grip.
column6: 什么……！？乌尔里克把我出卖了……！？{w}\n我转身想逃，可他立刻抓住了我的左臂。{w}\n我满心恐惧，力气不足以挣脱他的钳制。

column5: You've done nothing but bring an armed enemy into our home.\nWhat makes you think we can trust you? This is surely a trap.\nAs long as The Monarch can wield that blade, they are a threat.
column6: 你所做的不过是把一名全副武装的敌人带进了我们的家。\n你凭什么认为我们能信任你？这必定是个陷阱。\n只要君主还能使用那把剑，他们就是威胁。

column5: Ulric scoffs.
column6: 乌尔里克嗤笑一声。

column5: Then let me fix that.
column6: 那就让我来解决这个问题。

column5: A second after, Ulric phases the blade into his hands.{w}\nThen, much to my regret, he slices through my arm with ease.{w}\nI scream, and then from the elbow down, almost nothing remains.
column6: 一秒之后，乌尔里克将剑实体化到手中。{w}\n紧接着，令我悔恨不已的是，他轻而易举地斩断了我的手臂。{w}\n我放声尖叫，而从手肘往下，几乎什么也没剩下。

column5: There. Look how easy that was.\nNever again can that blade be used against you.\nNow do what I said. Surrender, and leave this world.
column6: 好了。看，多简单。\n那把剑再也不可能被用来对付你们了。\n现在照我说的做。投降，然后离开这个世界。

column5: I don't feel anything, almost as if my body numbs itself from the trauma.{w}\nBut the sight is all too real. My lower arm, limp, and dead on the floor.{w}\nBlood spurts from the wound, and I look at Ulric in disbelief.
column6: 我什么都感觉不到，仿佛身体因创伤而麻木了。{w}\n可眼前的景象却无比真实。我的小臂软弱无力地瘫死在地上。{w}\n鲜血从伤口喷涌而出，我难以置信地看向乌尔里克。

column5: He makes direct eye contact with me, and then looks at the torch.{w}\nI'm still gripping it tightly, and that's when things make sense.{w}\nWas he trying to fool them? I still have use of my good arm.
column6: 他直视着我的眼睛，随后看向那支火把。{w}\n我仍旧紧紧握着它，就在那时，我明白了一切。{w}\n他是在骗他们吗？我那条完好的手臂还能用。

column5: I slump against the wall, and use the torch to burn the wound shut.{w}\nA disgusting smell fills the air, and I can hear cracking and sizzling.{w}\nThis is all I can do, while I watch Ulric ascend the stairs with the blade.
column6: 我瘫靠在墙上，用火把将伤口烧灼封住。{w}\n一股恶臭弥漫在空气中，我能听见噼啪的灼烧声。{w}\n眼看着乌尔里克带着那把剑登上阶梯，我能做的也只有这些了。

column5: How surprising. You've changed, Ulric.\nWe thought your allegiance to The Rebellion was absolute.
column6: 真令人意外。你变了，乌尔里克。\n我们以为你对反抗军的忠诚是绝对的。

column5: No. It's my allegiance to Alestia that takes priority.\nThis senseless war will only end up destroying the world.\nOne life means nothing to me if it allows this land to flourish.
column6: 不。我优先效忠的是阿莱斯蒂亚。\n这场毫无意义的战争只会毁掉这个世界。\n若能换来这片土地的繁荣，一条性命对我而言算不了什么。

column5: The Triumvir looks down at my scabbard.{w}\nThey definitely believe Ulric removed my dominant arm.{w}\nI don't know why any of this is happening, but I let it all unfold.
column6: 执政官低头看了看我的剑鞘。{w}\n他们显然相信乌尔里克斩断的是我的惯用手臂。{w}\n我不知道这一切为何会发生，但我任由它发展下去。

column5: I trust Ulric, and I know he's doing this for a reason.
column6: 我信任乌尔里克，我知道他这么做自有理由。

column5: A generous offer, but one we cannot accept.\nSurely you know the truth now, after everything you've seen.\nThe Monarchy, and those that follow their path, lead worlds to ruin.
column6: 一份慷慨的提议，但我们无法接受。\n见过这一切之后，你现在总该知道真相了。\n王室，以及所有追随其道路的人，只会将世界引向毁灭。

column5: Ulric continues up the stairs, gripping the blade as tight as he can.
column6: 乌尔里克继续向阶梯上走去，尽可能紧地握着那把剑。

column5: We request that you join us once more, Ulric.\nIt would appear that Halin, Shane, and Sovy have let us down.\nYou can make the right choice. Join our ranks, and save the world.
column6: 我们请求你再次加入我们，乌尔里克。\n看来哈林、肖恩和索维都让我们失望了。\n你可以做出正确的选择。加入我们的行列，拯救这个世界。

column5: Ulric lets out a loud sigh, like he's considering their offer.
column6: 乌尔里克重重叹了口气，像是在考虑他们的提议。

column5: And what would you have me do...?
column6: 那你们想让我做什么……？

column5: As he speaks, he reaches the top of the stairs, and faces The Triumvir.{w}\nBy now, I'm almost coherent again, and the wound bleeds no more. Burnt shut.{w}\nI watch the two of them converse, wondering what exactly is going to happen.
column6: 他说着，走到了阶梯顶端，面对着那位执政官。{w}\n此时，我几乎恢复了清醒，伤口也不再流血了。已经被灼烧封住。{w}\n我看着他们两人交谈，心里琢磨着究竟会发生什么。

column5: Kneel, and pledge your loyalty to our cause.\nThen, turn that blade on The Monarch, and take his soul.\nThere's a reason we need both his power, and that blade.
column6: 跪下，宣誓效忠我们的事业。\n然后，把那把剑转向君主，取走他的灵魂。\n我们需要他的力量，也需要那把剑，这是有原因的。

column5: If you can do that, then all will be forgiven. \nYou see, Ulric — [firstname] is key to saving us all.\nHe would waste his power, while we plan to harness it correctly.
column6: 如果你能做到，那么一切都既往不咎。\n你看，乌尔里克——[firstname]是拯救我们所有人的关键。\n他会浪费自己的力量，而我们则打算正确地驾驭它。

column5: Kneel, and pledge your loyalty to our cause.\nThen, turn that blade on The Monarch, and take her soul.\nThere's a reason we need both her power, and that blade.
column6: 跪下，宣誓效忠我们的事业。\n然后，把那把剑转向君主，取走她的灵魂。\n我们需要她的力量，也需要那把剑，这是有原因的。

column5: If you can do that, then all will be forgiven.\nYou see, Ulric — [firstname] is key to saving us all.\nShe would waste her power, while we plan to harness it correctly.
column6: 如果你能做到，那么一切都既往不咎。\n你看，乌尔里克——[firstname]是拯救我们所有人的关键。\n她会浪费自己的力量，而我们则打算正确地驾驭它。

column5: What do you mean?
column6: 你这话是什么意思？

column5: Do as we say, and we will tell you everything.\nEven the things we could not tell you in the past.
column6: 照我们说的做，我们就会把一切都告诉你。\n甚至是那些过去我们无法告诉你的事。

column5: Ulric immediately drops the blade to his side, and kneels down.{w}\nIt hits the ground with a loud metallic clang, then rests there, motionless.
column6: 乌尔里克立刻将剑垂到身侧，跪了下来。{w}\n剑落在地上，发出一声铿锵的金属巨响，随后静止不动地躺在那儿。

column5: Good. We are glad that you realized the error of your ways.\nSiding with The Rebellion is foolish. It is a waste of your talent.\nWith us, you will finally be back on the right side of history.
column6: 很好。我们很高兴你认识到了自己的错误。\n站在反抗军那一边是愚蠢的。那是在浪费你的才能。\n和我们一起，你终将重新站到历史的正确一方。

column5: Yes, Master. Of course. My loyalty is forever yours.\nAs The Grand Inquisitor, I have only one goal.\nTo remove any threat that faces the throne.
column6: 是，主人。当然。我的忠诚永远属于您。\n作为大审判官，我只有一个目标。\n清除任何威胁王座的存在。

column5: Ulric grins as he says those words.
column6: 乌尔里克说这话时咧嘴一笑。

column5: Starting with you...
column6: 就从你们开始……

column5: A moment later, the blade disappears from the ground.{w}\nBut it doesn't return to Ulric's hands, or even mine.{w}\nIt phases directly through the chest of The Triumvir.
column6: 片刻之后，地上的剑消失了。{w}\n但它没有回到乌尔里克手中，也没有回到我的手中。{w}\n它径直穿过了那位执政官的胸膛。

column5: U-Ulric...!?
column6: 乌、乌尔里克……！？

column5: He rises to his feet, and grips the handle of the blade.{w}\nI knew I could trust him. I knew he had a plan...!{w}\nI'm so thankful that he wasn't betraying me.
column6: 他站起身来，握住剑柄。{w}\n我就知道我可以信任他。我就知道他自有打算……！{w}\n我多么庆幸他并不是在背叛我。

column5: You think I believed you...? Foolish, as always.\nYou let your guard down at the first sign of obedience.\nThe right side of history? Don't make me laugh.
column6: 你以为我相信了你……？还和从前一样愚蠢。\n一见到顺从的迹象，你们就放松了警惕。\n历史的正确一方？别逗我笑了。

column5: Ulric...
column6: 乌尔里克……

column5: You used a powerful blade in order to play God.\nBut now it's in the hands of [firstname]. A righteous man.\nHe will undo all that you've done — and {i}liberate{/i} Alestia.
column6: 你们利用一把强大的剑来扮演神明。\n可现在它握在[firstname]手中。一个正直的人。\n他会推翻你们所做的一切——并{i}解放{/i}阿莱斯蒂亚。

column5: You used a powerful blade in order to play God.\nBut now it's in the hands of The Monarch. A righteous woman.\nShe will undo all that you've done — and {i}liberate{/i} Alestia.
column6: 你们利用一把强大的剑来扮演神明。\n可现在它握在君主手中。一个正直的女子。\n她会推翻你们所做的一切——并{i}解放{/i}阿莱斯蒂亚。

column5: A moment later, he pulls out the blade.
column6: 片刻之后，他拔出了剑。

column5: You've held the world in chains for far too long.\nAnd now — it's finally time that they were broken.
column6: 你们用锁链束缚这个世界已经太久了。\n而现在——终于到了砸碎锁链的时候。

column5: Then, with a harsh kick, The Triumvir flies off the edge.{w}\nI can hear them scream as they fall, and then, the screams fade.{w}\nI'm in complete disbelief. He killed one of them? Was it truly that easy?
column6: 接着，一脚狠狠踢出，那位执政官飞出了边缘。{w}\n我能听见他们坠落时的惨叫，随后，那叫声渐渐消散。{w}\n我完全无法相信。他杀掉了他们中的一个？真有这么容易吗？

column5: Ulric drops the blade to the ground, and I summon it back into my grip.{w}\nAs I make my way up the stairs, my anger toward him is very clear.
column6: 乌尔里克把剑丢在地上，我将它召回手中。{w}\n当我向阶梯上走去时，我对他的怒气毫不掩饰。

column5: Look, I had to do it. A direct attack would've been suicide.\nWe had to make them lower their guard, and think that they were winning.\nAn act of betrayal, and a pledge of fealty? It's all I could think of doing.
column6: 听着，我不得不那么做。正面进攻无异于自杀。\n我们得让他们放松警惕，以为胜券在握。\n假意背叛，再宣誓效忠？这是我能想到的唯一办法。

column5: I start to speak, but he cuts me off immediately.
column6: 我刚要开口，就被他立刻打断了。

column5: I don't care what you have to say. Not right now.\nGet in those chambers, and finish this once and for all.\nThere's still two left, and you're only giving them time to prepare.
column6: 我不在乎你想说什么。现在不想听。\n进议事厅去，把这桩事彻底了结。\n还剩两个，你只是在给他们时间准备。

column5: With a sigh of regret, I realize that there's nothing I can do.{w}\nI sheathe the blade, and slowly enter The Triumvirate's chambers.{w}\nWe'd have plenty of time to talk later. I had to see this through to the end.
column6: 我遗憾地叹了口气，意识到自己什么也做不了。{w}\n我收起剑，缓缓走进三人执政团的议事厅。{w}\n我们以后有的是时间谈。我必须把这件事坚持到底。

column5: Either the end of The Triumvirate, or the end of myself...
column6: 要么是三人执政团的终结，要么是我自己的终结……

column5: When I enter their chambers, it looks just like I remember it.{w}\nI've been here before. I've had visions of standing in this very spot.{w}\nIn those visions, I remember walking toward the idol in the back.
column6: 当我走进他们的议事厅时，这里和我记忆中的一模一样。{w}\n我来过这里。我曾有过站在这个位置的幻象。{w}\n在那些幻象里，我记得自己走向后方的灵像。

column5: I can feel the blade respond to this room, but I'm not sure why.{w}\nIt's not moving or anything — it's just a feeling deep in my gut.{w}\nAs I go to grab the blade, I hear a loud voice call out to me.
column6: 我能感觉到那把剑对这个房间起了反应，却不知为何。{w}\n它并没有动——只是我内心深处的一种直觉。{w}\n正当我要去握那把剑时，我听见一个响亮的声音朝我呼喊。

column5: Stop.
column6: 住手。

column5: Then, out of nowhere, I see two cloaks appear by the idol.{w}\nOne of them stays in place, and the other walks toward me.{w}\nThe one at the back was surely my target, and their leader.
column6: 紧接着，不知从哪里冒出两件斗篷，出现在灵像旁。{w}\n其中一个留在原地，另一个朝我走来。{w}\n后面那个无疑是我的目标，也是他们的首领。

column5: Do not draw that blade unless you intend to use it.\nThat idol will respond to your aggression, and fight back.\nWe will not harm you. We brought you here for another reason.
column6: 除非你打算动手，否则别拔出那把剑。\n那尊灵像会对你的敌意作出反应，并且反击。\n我们不会伤害你。我们把你带到这里，另有原因。

column5: Another reason...? What could it be?{w}\nI know I was told not to let them speak, but I'm curious.{w}\nAssuming a neutral stance, I ask them to explain themselves.
column6: 另有原因……？会是什么呢？{w}\n我知道有人告诫过我别让他们开口，可我很好奇。{w}\n我摆出中立的姿态，让他们解释清楚。

column5: That is a tall order, Monarch.
column6: 这可是个过分的要求，君主。

column5: I notice they use my proper title.{w}\nIn this moment, there was no room left for doubt.{w}\nEverything Howl told us about The Triumvirate was true.
column6: 我注意到他们用了我的正式头衔。{w}\n这一刻，再没有任何怀疑的余地。{w}\n豪尔告诉我们的关于三人执政团的一切都是真的。

column5: They don't speak, they just stand there in silence.{w}\nIf I had anything to ask them, I guess now would be the time to do it.{w}\nHowever, earlier warnings echo in my ears. Warnings against letting them speak.
column6: 他们没有开口，只是沉默地站在那里。{w}\n如果我有想问的，我想现在正是时候。{w}\n然而，先前的告诫在我耳中回响。那是别让他们开口的告诫。

column5: We are nobody, and yet we are everyone.\nWe are the same, and yet we are different.\nThere is really no way to answer that question.
column6: 我们谁都不是，却又无所不是。\n我们彼此相同，却又各不相同。\n那个问题，实在无从回答。

column5: Like you, we are simply beings capable of wielding that blade.\nWhen the sun sets on this era, and rises again, we will be forgotten.\nReduced to cosmic dust, we will become even less than a memory.
column6: 和你一样，我们不过是能够驾驭那把剑的存在。\n当这个时代的太阳落下又升起时，我们就会被遗忘。\n化为宇宙的尘埃，我们将连记忆都算不上。

column5: It matters not how the cycle ends. Only how the cycle began.\nThe ones who created that blade could never comprehend what they started.\nAn endless war of life against death — of purity against corruption.
column6: 这个循环如何终结并不重要。重要的是它如何开始。\n创造那把剑的人永远无法理解自己启动了怎样的东西。\n一场生与死、纯洁与腐化之间无休无止的战争。

column5: As long as that blade exists, there will be beings capable of wielding it.\nAnd as long as those beings exist, they will inevitably meet, just like us.\nA catalyst for the clashing of ideals. It exists only to create disorder.
column6: 只要那把剑存在，就会有能够驾驭它的存在。\n而只要那些存在存在，他们就终将相遇，就像我们一样。\n它是理念冲突的催化剂。它存在的意义，就是制造混乱。

column5: Long ago, a group of three, faced an almost insurmountable foe.\nThey were able to prevail, and they thought that they had won peace.\nAll of the worlds, once closed off, became united in one large universe.
column6: 很久以前，三个人面对着一个几乎无法战胜的敌人。\n他们取得了胜利，以为赢得了和平。\n所有彼此隔绝的世界，从此连成了一个庞大的宇宙。

column5: You see, that blade was created from the clashing of conflicting ideals.\nLife against death, purity against corruption. It feeds off of that imbalance.\nWhat they held after the battle, was only a portend of more strife to come.
column6: 你看，那把剑诞生于相互冲突的理念的碰撞。\n生与死，纯洁与腐化。它靠那种失衡为食。\n战后他们手中所持的，不过是更多纷争将至的预兆。

column5: We do look fondly on those who created the blade, but we also hate them.\nWere it not for them, neither of us would be standing here right now.\nBut because of them, we stand here at odds, instead of peace.
column6: 我们对创造那把剑的人既怀有眷恋，也心怀憎恨。\n若不是他们，我们双方此刻都不会站在这里。\n可正因为他们，我们才站在这里彼此为敌，而非共享和平。

column5: Memories of their exploits linger through the core of that blade.\nBut no matter how strong they were, one fact remained.\nThey were nothing but foolish men.
column6: 他们事迹的记忆仍萦绕在那把剑的核心之中。\n但无论他们多么强大，有一个事实始终不变。\n他们不过是些愚蠢的人。

column5: Men who thought themselves worthy of delivering justice.
column6: 自以为有资格施行正义的人。

column5: Men, who with all the power in the world, still remained short-sighted.
column6: 手握世间一切力量，却依旧目光短浅的人。

column5: They knew not what they trifled with, Monarch. \nThey thought that the blade was a symbol of victory, but no.\nAfter what you've been through, we both know what it truly means.
column6: 他们不知道自己玩弄的是什么，君主。\n他们以为那把剑是胜利的象征，但并非如此。\n经历过这一切之后，你我都清楚它真正的含义。

column5: War, and death...
column6: 战争，与死亡……

column5: Well, true evil can almost never be fully defeated.\nThough heroes of the past stood victorious over evil, it was temporary.\nIn the future, sometimes even millions of years ahead — the evil returned.
column6: 真正的邪恶，几乎永远无法被彻底消灭。\n尽管昔日的英雄曾战胜邪恶，那也只是暂时的。\n在未来，有时甚至是在数百万年之后——邪恶卷土重来。

column5: And now it stands before you, corrupting the very heart of Alestia.\nBut this is not the first world it has harmed; and it plans to keep moving.\nWe follow it, with that blade, and save innocent worlds from its wrath.
column6: 如今它就在你面前，侵蚀着阿莱斯蒂亚的心脏。\n但它祸害过的世界不止这一个，它还打算继续前行。\n我们带着那把剑追随它，从它的怒火中拯救无辜的世界。

column5: Look at the dying Balteus. It would deliver that fate to every single world.\nRather than temporarily cast the idol away, we decided to settle down on this planet.\nOur goal was to find a way to destroy both the idol, and the blade, for good.
column6: 看看正在衰亡的巴尔泰乌斯。它会把同样的命运带给每一个世界。\n与其暂时驱走那尊灵像，我们决定在这个星球定居下来。\n我们的目标是找到一种办法，将灵像和那把剑一并永久摧毁。

column5: Doing so would liberate the universe from this eternal war.\nBut we did not hold the power required to destroy the idol. Not yet.\nIf we could make the blade stronger, though, then we might stand a chance.
column6: 这样做便能让宇宙从这场永恒的战争中解脱。\n但我们并不拥有摧毁那尊灵像所需的力量。至少当时还没有。\n可如果我们能让那把剑变得更强，或许就有一线希望。

column5: If it could match the strength of the idol, then that could be it.\nThe energy unleashed in such a moment, would destroy both for sure.\nSince the blade fed on life — we would have to start relying on others.
column6: 如果它能与灵像的力量匹敌，那或许就能成事。\n那一刻释放的能量，必定会将两者一同摧毁。\n既然那把剑以生命为食——我们就不得不开始依靠他人。

column5: They had planned to use this idol as a source of power.\nPerhaps to aid in their conquest of other worlds.\nThe universe belonged to them, they thought.
column6: 他们本打算把这尊灵像当作力量的来源。\n或许是为了助他们征服其他世界。\n在他们看来，宇宙本就属于他们。

column5: But wielding the power of evil incarnate would only lead to ruin.\nWe couldn't let them continue down a path as dangerous as that.\nSo we cast them aside, in an astral prison, using that blade.
column6: 可掌控邪恶化身的只会招致毁灭。\n我们不能让他们继续走在那样危险的道路上。\n于是我们用那把剑，将他们放逐进了一座星界牢狱。

column5: And as we did, we created new life on Alestia.\nA new, pure species, that would keep on reproducing.\nA breeding ground of power for that blade to harvest.
column6: 与此同时，我们在阿莱斯蒂亚创造了新的生命。\n一个全新的、纯洁的种族，会不断繁衍。\n一片为那把剑提供力量的培育之地。

column5: If we could make that blade strong enough, then we'd win.\nBut even then, we couldn't gather power fast enough.\nThe idol started corrupting, and killing Balteus.
column6: 如果我们能让那把剑足够强大，我们就能取胜。\n可即便如此，我们聚集力量的速度还是太慢。\n那尊灵像开始腐化，并夺走巴尔泰乌斯的生机。

column5: We had to think of something, and fast.\nIt led us down a path that we did not want to walk.\nBut in order to create peace — it was necessary.
column6: 我们必须尽快想出办法。\n它把我们引上了一条我们并不想走的路。\n可为了缔造和平——这是必须的。

column5: We are not surprised, given our method of harvesting power.\nYou see, this is not the first time you have stood in our chambers.\nHopefully, it is the last. But to be honest, we've seen you many times.
column6: 考虑到我们收集力量的方式，我们并不感到意外。\n你看，这并非你第一次站在我们的议事厅里。\n但愿这是最后一次。但说实话，我们已见过你许多次了。

column5: That blade exists unbound from the restraints of time and space.\nEvery death along your journey has only served to power it further.\nWhen you got here, if it was not strong enough, we sent you back.
column6: 那把剑不受时间与空间的束缚。\n你旅途中的每一次死亡，都只是让它变得更强。\n当你来到这里，如果它还不够强大，我们就把你送回去。

column5: When we did so, the blade remained unchanged.\nThe cycle started anew, giving that weapon even more strength.\nYou stand here, the result of millions of years worth of trial and error.
column6: 我们那样做时，那把剑依旧如故。\n循环重新开始，让那件武器获得了更强的力量。\n你站在这里，是数百万年无数次试错的成果。

column5: The Occupation, The Rebellion, and even your attack on Balteus...\nWe created a period of time in your history filled with nothing but death.\nOver, and over, you and your friends have lived it. Only to power that blade.
column6: 那场占领，那场反抗，甚至是你对巴尔泰乌斯的进攻……\n我们在你们的历史中制造了一段只有死亡的时期。\n你和你的朋友们一遍又一遍地经历它。只为给那把剑注入力量。

column5: When the final cycle came along, we would have you carry out your goal.\nThe destruction of both the idol, and the sword, is what you were meant for.\nYou may have come to kill us, but your virtues are simply misplaced.
column6: 当最后的循环到来时，我们便会让你去完成你的使命。\n摧毁灵像和那把剑，正是你存在的意义。\n你也许是来杀我们的，但你的一身美德只是用错了地方。

column5: Nothing does. Well at least, not at first.\nOriginally, we hoped that our champion would come from Alarinthia.\nThat's why we kept that nation separate, and focused on strength.
column6: 什么都算不上。至少一开始是这样。\n最初，我们希望我们的斗士会出自阿拉林西亚。\n所以我们让那个国家保持独立，并专注于力量。

column5: If each ruler was stronger then the last...?\nWell, as time passed, we might find someone strong enough.\nSomeone with the will, {i}and{/i} power required to wield that blade.
column6: 如果每一位统治者都比前一位更强……？\n那么随着时间流逝，我们或许能找到足够强大的人。\n一个既有意志、{i}又{/i}有驾驭那把剑所需力量的人。

column5: Of course, it became clear that this would never work.\nJust as we started to give up hope, those idols appeared.\nThe Monarchy was somehow able to reach out of their prison.
column6: 当然，事实证明这永远行不通。\n就在我们开始放弃希望时，那些灵像出现了。\n王室不知用什么方法从牢狱中伸出了手。

column5: The growing nation of Valinorth developed their culture around this.\nAnd as a reward for reverence, the concept of The Seer was created.\nA special citizen of Valinorth, with the power of The Monarchy inside of them.
column6: 日益壮大的瓦利诺斯围绕着这一点发展出了自己的文化。\n而作为虔诚的奖赏，先知这一概念被创造了出来。\n一位瓦利诺斯的特殊公民，体内寄宿着王室的力量。

column5: Even then, none of these Seers were as strong as we needed.\nUntil you. The Monarchy gave you everything they had.\nWe assume that they did this so you would kill us.
column6: 即便如此，这些先知中没有一个强大到我们需要的程度。\n直到你出现。王室把他们的一切都给了你。\n我们猜想，他们这样做是为了让你来杀死我们。

column5: But it would seem that they played right into our hands.\nYou were led down a path that only gave you more and more power.\nIn all of the universe, you are the only one who can use that blade effectively.
column6: 但看来他们恰好落入了我们的算计。\n你被引上了一条只会让你愈发强大的道路。\n在整个宇宙中，你是唯一能够有效使用那把剑的人。

column5: You house not just your own will, but the will of billions of spirits.\nSpirits that want nothing more than to see their homeworld freed.\nThere was no other choice, really. You are our champion, Monarch.
column6: 你体内承载的不只是你自己的意志，还有数十亿灵的意志。\n那些灵只想看到自己的故土获得自由。\n实在没有别的选择。你就是我们的斗士，君主。

column5: No. You are our creation, and you must do as we say.\nBut your actions, will ensure peace and happiness for trillions.\nIt is a small price to pay, and we know that you would agree.
column6: 不。你是我们的造物，你必须照我们说的做。\n而你的行动，将确保数万亿生灵的和平与幸福。\n这是微不足道的代价，我们知道你也会同意。

column5: We wish to end a cycle that has plagued the universe for eternities.\nIn fact, it could be even longer. It is impossible to know for sure.\nBecause of that, we believe that no price is too high to pay.
column6: 我们想终结一个困扰宇宙无数纪元的循环。\n事实上，它可能还要更久。根本无法确知。\n正因如此，我们相信任何代价都不算高。

column5: We will never be remembered. Nobody will ever know our sacrifice.\nBut there shall never be another world marred by that corrupt idol.\nAnd no men will ever again be seduced by the power of that blade.
column6: 我们永远不会被记住。没有人会知道我们的牺牲。\n但再也不会有世界被那尊腐化的灵像所摧残。\n也再不会有人被那把剑的力量所蛊惑。

column5: The best course of action for the universe is to destroy them both.\nTheir existence will always lead to those who believe they control fate.\nThey will always lead to a clash of ideals, and will always lead to {i}this{/i}.
column6: 对宇宙而言，最好的做法就是将两者一同摧毁。\n它们的存在总会催生出妄图掌控命运之人。\n它们总会引发理念的冲突，总会导向{i}这般{/i}结局。

column5: That was enough talk. I came here to kill them, and that's what I'd do.{w}\nNo matter what they had to say, they couldn't talk themselves free.{w}\nThey hurt my world, and my friends. I would make them suffer.
column6: 说得够多了。我来这里就是为了杀他们，我就要这么做。{w}\n无论他们有什么话要说，都别想靠嘴皮子逃过一劫。{w}\n他们伤害了我的世界，我的朋友们。我要让他们痛苦。

column5: The mind can suffer when stuck in the same time and place.\nHistory repeating itself can be far more than maddening.\nWe try to break free from the cycle, but only perish.
column6: 当心智被困在同一个时间与地点时，是会受苦的。\n历史不断重演，足以令人发疯。\n我们试图挣脱这个循环，却只会一次次消亡。

column5: This member of The Triumvirate is talking so differently.{w}\nThe one back in the previous room had almost a completely different story.{w}\nIf being caught in a cycle could drive them mad, I had to wonder {i}which{/i} one was mad.
column6: 这位三人执政团的成员说话的方式截然不同。{w}\n上一个房间里那位讲的故事几乎完全不一样。{w}\n如果困在循环中会让人发疯，那我不得不琢磨{i}哪一个{/i}才是疯的。

column5: This is why we will not stop you if you wish to kill us.\nThat blade has kept us alive long enough to see things through.\nOur final rest, would only be a sign that we have finally won.
column6: 这就是为什么你若想杀我们，我们不会阻拦。\n那把剑让我们活了下来，久到足以把一切看到最后。\n我们的长眠，只会是我们终于获胜的标志。

column5: So go ahead. Kill me, and kill my Master.\nTurn that blade on the idol, and see what happens.\nSee if you can finally free everybody from its wrath.
column6: 所以，动手吧。杀了我，再杀了我的主人。\n把那把剑转向灵像，看看会发生什么。\n看看你是否终于能让所有人从它的怒火中解脱。

column5: Not just us, or Alestia. But all worlds, and all people.\nIf you are not strong enough, then the cycle will just start anew.\nBefore you know it, you may be facing us here once more.
column6: 不只是我们，也不只是阿莱斯蒂亚。而是所有的世界，所有的生灵。\n如果你不够强大，那么循环只会重新开始。\n不知不觉间，你或许又会在这里与我们相见。

column5: But know that we are not your enemy.\nAll we've done, we've done to—
column6: 但你要知道，我们并非你的敌人。\n我们所做的一切，都是为了——

column5: I'm sick of hearing it. I'm sick of this weak justification.{w}\nI phase the blade into my hand, and thrust it through their chest.{w}\nBut like I was warned before, the idol responds to my aggression.
column6: 我听腻了。我听腻了这种苍白的辩解。{w}\n我将剑实体化到手中，刺穿了他们的胸膛。{w}\n但正如先前有人警告我的那样，那尊灵像回应了我的敌意。

column5: The room is engulfed in a blinding darkness.{w}\nIt must be the idol. The blade usually causes a {i}white{/i} light.{w}\nI feel immense warmth around me, and hear the crackling of flames.
column6: 房间被一片令人目眩的黑暗吞没。{w}\n一定是那尊灵像。那把剑通常会迸发出{i}白色{/i}的光芒。{w}\n我感到周围涌来巨大的热浪，听见火焰噼啪作响。

column5: The darkness fades, and the entire room is engulfed in fire.{w}\nThe Triumvir stands before me, bleeding, and crying.{w}\nThese were no Gods. Just weak, arrogant people.
column6: 黑暗褪去，整个房间被烈火吞没。{w}\n那位执政官站在我面前，流着血，哭泣着。{w}\n他们根本不是神。只是一群软弱又傲慢的人。

column5: V-very well...
column6: 很、很好……

column5: I turn left, and face the flames, forcefully taking them with me.{w}\nI hold them there, with the blade, tempted to absorb their soul.{w}\nBut no, they don't deserve it. They don't deserve the satisfaction.
column6: 我转向左边，面朝火焰，强行将他们一起拖了过去。{w}\n我用剑把他们按在那里，一时动了吸走他们灵魂的念头。{w}\n但不。他们不配。他们不配得到这种满足。

column5: I pull the blade out, and watch as the wound oozes blood.{w}\nThen, I grab them by the cloak, and pull them close to me.{w}\nIn their final moments, I curse them, and condemn them.
column6: 我拔出剑，看着伤口渗出血来。{w}\n接着，我抓住他们的斗篷，把他们拉近身前。{w}\n在他们生命的最后时刻，我诅咒他们，斥责他们。

column5: And then I push them back into the idol's flames.{w}\nI hear them scream, and writhe as they're slowly burned alive.{w}\nIn my opinion, they deserved a punishment far worse than that.
column6: 然后我把他们推回灵像的火焰中。{w}\n我听见他们的惨叫与挣扎，被活活慢慢烧死。{w}\n在我看来，他们配得上的惩罚要远比这更重。

column5: Now — just one more to go...
column6: 现在——只剩最后一个了……

column5: As I turn back to face the idol, the final triumvir stands before me.{w}\nI hold out the blade toward them, showing my intent to kill.{w}\nThat was my goal. Kill The Triumvirate. Destroy the idol.
column6: 当我转身再次面向灵像时，最后一位执政官站在了我面前。{w}\n我举剑指向他们，表明我的杀意。{w}\n那就是我的目标。杀死三人执政团。摧毁灵像。

column5: Stop...! Think about what you're doing!\nEverything we've done, we've done in the name of freedom!
column6: 住手……！想想你在做什么！\n我们所做的一切，都是以自由之名！

column5: They get down on their knees, and look up at me.
column6: 他们跪了下来，抬头看着我。

column5: Normally, I'd send you back to start the cycle anew.\nBut now — your strength surpasses mine. This {i}must{/i} be the end.\nI beg for your mercy. Let me live to see what I've fought for...!
column6: 换作平常，我会把你送回去，让循环重新开始。\n但现在——你的力量已超越了我。这{i}一定{/i}就是终局了。\n我求你开恩。让我活着看到我为之奋斗的一切……！

column5: Without hesitation, I swing the blade, and cut off their head.{w}\nThey fall to the ground, and blood stains the white of their cloak.{w}\nI'm not sure what to believe, as they all had something different to say.
column6: 我毫不犹豫地挥剑，斩下了他们的头颅。{w}\n他们倒在地上，鲜血染红了他们洁白的斗篷。{w}\n我不知道该相信什么，因为他们每个人说的都不一样。

column5: Perhaps they meant to use that doubt as a weapon when I got here.{w}\nI throw away that nonsense, and stick to the goal I originally had.{w}\nWith them out of the way, it was time to destroy that idol for good.
column6: 也许他们本就打算在我来到这里时，把这份疑虑当作武器。{w}\n我抛开这些无稽之谈，坚持我最初的目标。{w}\n既然他们已不成阻碍，是时候将那尊灵像彻底摧毁了。

column5: I take a step forward, and my body is assaulted with pain.{w}\nI can tell that the idol is fighting back, and I fall to my knees.{w}\nThe flames are so hot that I feel as if I'm melting away, too.
column6: 我向前迈出一步，剧痛便侵袭了我的身体。{w}\n我能感觉到那尊灵像在反击，我跪倒在地。{w}\n火焰炽热得让我觉得自己也快要熔化了。

column5: But no, something else is happening. It's not just the flames.{w}\nThe idol is trying to kill me — but I'm not the only one here.{w}\nInside of me is The Monarchy. Billions of spirits, wanting to help.
column6: 但不，还有别的事情在发生。不只是火焰。{w}\n那尊灵像想要杀我——可在这里的不止我一个。{w}\n我的体内是王室。数十亿渴望相助的灵。

column5: It's almost as if they're shielding me. Sacrificing themselves for me.{w}\nI stand up, and take another step forward. The pain is even worse.{w}\nI fall to my hands and knees, and cry in agony. It's too much...!
column6: 仿佛他们在为我遮挡。为我牺牲自己。{w}\n我站起身来，又向前迈出一步。疼痛更加剧烈。{w}\n我四肢着地倒了下去，痛苦地哀嚎。太过了……！

column5: My vision blurs, but after a while, things return to normal.{w}\nThough the pain has gone away, I start to feel weaker and weaker.{w}\nI know that the souls inside of me are giving their lives for this.
column6: 我的视线模糊了，但过了一阵，一切又恢复正常。{w}\n尽管疼痛已经消退，我却开始感到越来越虚弱。{w}\n我知道，我体内的灵魂正为此献出生命。

column5: If I could get to the idol, and attack it, I might be able to win.{w}\nThat was a big maybe. But there was {i}one{/i} thing I knew for sure.{w}\nI might not live through this, and there was no other option.
column6: 如果我能靠近那尊灵像并攻击它，或许就能赢。{w}\n那是个很大的“或许”。但有{i}一件事{/i}我确定无疑。{w}\n我可能活不过这一遭，而除此之外别无选择。

column5: Every step I took — could easily be my last.
column6: 我迈出的每一步——都可能成为最后一步。

column5: I take one more step, and ready the blade.{w}\nAs soon as I thrust it into that idol, things would be over.{w}\nBut as the power within me dwindled, I realized one thing.
column6: 我又迈出一步，握紧了剑。{w}\n一旦我将它刺入那尊灵像，一切就都结束了。{w}\n可随着我体内的力量逐渐枯竭，我意识到了一件事。

column5: No matter what happened next, the blade would be destroyed.{w}\nBut if I wanted to get rid of the idol for good — then I would perish as well.{w}\nIn order to live, and see another day, I'd have to hold back — just a bit.
column6: 无论接下来发生什么，那把剑都会被摧毁。{w}\n可若我想彻底铲除那尊灵像——那我也将随之消亡。{w}\n若想活下来，看到明天的太阳，我就得留手——只需一点点。

column5: But if I did that, then there's a chance the idol might not be fully defeated.{w}\nIt could come back in the future, to corrupt and decay other innocent worlds.{w}\nWas keeping my life worth condemning other worlds to suffer like {i}we{/i} did...?
column6: 可如果我那样做，那尊灵像就有可能无法被彻底消灭。{w}\n它可能在未来卷土重来，腐蚀并摧毁其他无辜的世界。{w}\n为了保住我的性命，就要让别的世界承受{i}我们{/i}那样的苦难，值得吗……？

column5: I thrust the blade into the idol, and activate it. The blinding white light follows.{w}\nThis was the end. The blade, in mere moments, would enact my final will.{w}\nI just have to ask myself, what would that final will be...?
column6: 我将剑刺入那尊灵像，并激活了它。随即亮起令人目眩的白光。{w}\n这就是终局。那把剑将在片刻之后，执行我最终的意志。{w}\n我不禁自问，那最终的意志会是什么……？

column5: I had a world to rule. I couldn't just let myself die.{w}\nI was The Monarch, and I needed to live up to that role.{w}\nIf I died during this war, the world could be thrown into disarray.
column6: 我还有一整个世界要治理。我不能就这样让自己死去。{w}\n我是君主，我必须配得上这个身份。{w}\n如果我在这场战争中死去，世界可能会陷入混乱。

column5: At least, that's the justification that I give to myself.{w}\nI just know, that deep down inside, I deserve to see the world I fought for.{w}\nThat Triumvir wanted the same, but I denied them. What gave {i}me{/i} the right?
column6: 至少，这是我给自己找的借口。{w}\n我只知道，在内心深处，我值得看到我为之奋战的世界。{w}\n那位执政官也曾想要同样的东西，却是我拒绝了他。{i}我{/i}又凭什么这么做？

column5: I guess it didn't matter, now. I can feel myself fading away.{w}\nAfter I command the blade to conserve power, and save me, I close my eyes.{w}\nNo matter what happened to me, I could rest knowing one simple fact.
column6: 我想，现在这些都不重要了。我能感觉到自己正在消散。{w}\n在命令那把剑节省力量、保住我自己之后，我闭上了眼睛。{w}\n无论我会遭遇什么，我都能安心歇息，只需明白一个简单的事实。

column5: I couldn't spare myself if it meant that other worlds could be hurt.{w}\nIt would be selfish. Even though I wanted to live, I knew I couldn't.{w}\nAs soon as we set sail, I knew that this could be the end for me.
column6: 如果保全自己就意味着别的世界可能遭殃，那我做不到。{w}\n那太自私了。尽管我想活下去，但我知道我不能。{w}\n从我们起航的那一刻起，我就知道这可能就是我自己的终点。

column5: But even though I knew it was a possibility, I still didn't want to believe it.{w}\nI was only fooling myself, thinking that I could live to see what I fought for.{w}\nI denied The Triumvir that right, and now I would deny it to myself as well.
column6: 可即便知道这是一种可能，我依然不愿相信。{w}\n我一直在自欺欺人，以为自己能活着看到我为之奋战的一切。{w}\n我剥夺了那位执政官的这个权利，如今我也要剥夺自己的。

column5: I guess it didn't matter, now. I can feel myself fading away.{w}\nI command the blade to use all the power it can. Including that of my life.{w}\nNo matter what happened to me, I could rest knowing one simple fact.
column6: 我想，现在这些都不重要了。我能感觉到自己正在消散。{w}\n我命令那把剑用尽它所能用的一切力量。包括我的生命。{w}\n无论我会遭遇什么，我都能安心歇息，只需明白一个简单的事实。

column5: Alestia had been given the future that it deserved...{w}\nIn the hands of the people, they were free to live as they pleased.{w}\nAs everything fades away, I wonder what that future might bring my allies.
column6: 阿莱斯蒂亚已经得到了它应得的未来……{w}\n交到人民手中，他们得以自由地如愿生活。{w}\n当一切都渐渐消散，我思索着那个未来会给同伴们带来什么。

column5: I smile — a stark contrast to the tears streaming down my face.{w}\nWith another step, I'm almost facing the idol. I couldn't do this alone.{w}\nThe voices of my comrades, and the souls inside of me carry me forward.
column6: 我笑了——与脸上奔流而下的泪水形成鲜明对比。{w}\n再迈一步，我几乎正对着那尊灵像了。我一个人做不到这些。{w}\n同伴们的声音，以及我体内的灵魂，支撑着我向前。

column5: So, everything has led to this.\nThe Monarchy is no more, but you can still live.\nMake it through this — and give Alestia the future it deserves.
column6: 所以，一切都走到了这一步。\n王室已经不在了，但你还活着。\n挺过这一关——把阿莱斯蒂亚应得的未来交给它。

column5: I use the blade for support, and try to rise to my feet.{w}\nThis is taking so much out of me. Would I have enough power in the end?{w}\nHoping with every fiber of my being that I do — I take another step forward.
column6: 我拄着剑支撑身体，试图站起来。{w}\n这耗尽了我的力气。到最后我还会有足够的力量吗？{w}\n我倾尽全部身心祈祷自己还有，然后向前又迈出一步。

column5: I knew there was something special about you. Ever since the start.\nYou brought us all together — and unified us. You made us a family.
column6: 我就知道你很特别。从一开始就知道。\n你把我们聚在了一起——让我们团结一心。你让我们成了一家人。

column5: With another step, I fall right to the ground.{w}\nI lay there, crying, and squirming in pain.{w}\nMy grip on the blade tightens as I shake.
column6: 再迈一步，我径直摔倒在地。{w}\n我躺在那里，哭喊着，痛苦地扭动。{w}\n我浑身颤抖，握剑的手却更紧了。

column5: Is {i}this{/i} really how you want your story to be told...?\nGet up, [firstname]. Get up and finish what you started!
column6: 你{i}真的{/i}想让你的故事以这种方式被讲述吗……？\n站起来，[firstname]。站起来，把你开始的事做完！

column5: As the souls exit my body to shield me, I get noticeably weaker.{w}\nI tremble with every step, trying as hard as I can to keep myself standing.{w}\nMy comrades call out to me, and urge me to keep moving. I start to cry.
column6: 随着灵魂离开我的身体去为我遮挡，我明显地越来越虚弱。{w}\n我每走一步都在颤抖，拼尽全力让自己站住。{w}\n同伴们向我呼喊，催促我继续前行。我开始哭了起来。

column5: I guess I'm no longer the strongest member of The Rebellion.\nI'm proud of you, [firstname]. You saw this through to the bitter end.
column6: 看来我不再是反抗军中最强的人了。\n我为你骄傲，[firstname]。你把这桩事坚持到了苦涩的尽头。

column5: I'm not sure what I just heard, since nobody is actually around me.{w}\nIn these chambers, it would seem that time and space act abnormally.{w}\nWith another step, I grit my teeth. It feels like I'm being torn apart...!
column6: 我不确定自己刚才听见了什么，因为我身边其实空无一人。{w}\n在这间议事厅里，时间与空间似乎都失常了。{w}\n再迈一步，我咬紧牙关。感觉自己正被撕成碎片……！

column5: Keep on moving! We didn't come this far just to lose now!
column6: 继续走！我们走了这么远，可不是为了在此刻认输！

column5: Determination rises within me, and I take another step forward.{w}\nMy body is racked with pain, and it's almost impossible to walk.{w}\nI use the blade as a makeshift cane, as a voice sounds in my head.
column6: 决心在我心中升起，我又向前迈出一步。{w}\n剧痛折磨着我的身体，几乎寸步难行。{w}\n我把剑当作临时的拐杖，这时一个声音在我脑海中响起。

column5: You can do this, [firstname]...! Don't give up!
column6: 你能做到的，[firstname]……！别放弃！

column5: Valessa returned to Valinorth, accepting her mantle as Elder.\nLeading Valinorth in a way that respected its tradition, the nation flourished.\nBorders became less strict, and Valinorth was popular with tourists in the future.
column6: 瓦莱莎回到了瓦利诺斯，接受了长老的重任。\n她以尊重传统的方式领导瓦利诺斯，让这个国家繁荣兴旺。\n边境管制逐渐放宽，日后瓦利诺斯深受游客喜爱。

column5: Because of her wishes, and style of leadership — Valinorth retained its culture.\nForests were left intact, the idol was left standing, and everything was just as it was.\nGoing down in history as one of the most revered Elders, all future rulers respected her wishes.
column6: 由于她的意愿与领导风格——瓦利诺斯保留了自己的文化。\n森林保持原样，灵像依旧矗立，一切都如从前一般。\n她作为最受敬重的长老之一载入史册，此后的所有统治者都尊重她的遗愿。

column5: Though the distance between you was immense, your love flourished.\nFrequent visits going both ways ensured that your bond never weakened.\nFor when the love in one's heart is strong enough — nothing can stand in its way.
column6: 尽管你们相隔万里，你们的爱却愈发茁壮。\n频繁的相互探访让你们的情谊从未淡薄。\n因为当心中的爱足够坚定——任何事物都无法阻挡。

column5: That is, of course, except for the unforgiving flow of time.\nThough death would part the two of you, legends would speak of your near-eternal love.\nShe lived a long, full life. A wonderful reward for her duty and sacrifice, as most would say.
column6: 当然，除了那无情流逝的时光。\n尽管死亡终将把你们分开，传说仍会讲述你们近乎永恒的爱。\n她度过了漫长而充实的一生。正如大多数人所说，这是对她尽责与牺牲的美好回报。

column5: Valessa would stay in close contact with you throughout her lifetime.\nThough the distance between you was large, your bond was forever strong.\nVisits, as infrequent as they were — played out as if no time was lost at all.
column6: 瓦莱莎一生都与你保持着密切联系。\n尽管你们相隔遥远，你们的情谊却始终坚固。\n相聚虽不常有——却仿佛从未错过任何时光。

column5: But as dictated by time, all reigns must come to an end.\nValessa passed away peacefully, surrounded by friends and family.\nShe lived a long, full life. A wonderful reward for her former duty and sacrifice.
column6: 但正如时间所注定，一切统治终有尽头。\n瓦莱莎在亲友的环绕中安详离世。\n她度过了漫长而充实的一生。这是对她昔日尽责与牺牲的美好回报。

column5: Valessa started a new tradition to remember your love, and keep it alive.\nOnce a year, gifts and well wishes would be left at Sauleberg's idol.\nThis was to thank the idol that empowered you, and saved all of Alestia.
column6: 瓦莱莎开创了一项新的传统，以铭记并延续你们的爱。\n每年一次，人们会在索尔伯格的灵像前留下礼物与祝福。\n这是为了感谢那尊赋予你力量、拯救了整个阿莱斯蒂亚的灵像。

column5: For as long as she lived, she attended every year.\nKnown as a strong ruler, this was the only time she shed a tear.\nYour legacy, and your sacrifice, was honored by Valinorth forever.
column6: 只要她活着，每年都会到场。\n作为以坚强著称的统治者，这是她唯一落泪的时刻。\n你的遗志与牺牲，被瓦利诺斯永远铭记。

column5: Valessa started a new tradition in your honor.\nOnce a year, gifts and well wishes would be left at Sauleberg's idol.\nThis was to thank the idol that empowered you, and saved all of Alestia.
column6: 瓦莱莎为纪念你开创了一项新的传统。\n每年一次，人们会在索尔伯格的灵像前留下礼物与祝福。\n这是为了感谢那尊赋予你力量、拯救了整个阿莱斯蒂亚的灵像。

column5: For as long as she lived, she attended every year.\nKnown as a strong ruler, this was the only time she shed a tear.\nYour legacy, and your sacrifice, was honored by Valinorth forever.
column6: 只要她活着，每年都会到场。\n作为以坚强著称的统治者，这是她唯一落泪的时刻。\n你的遗志与牺牲，被瓦利诺斯永远铭记。

column5: After the war, Valessa dedicated her life to philanthropy.\nShe helped the people of Mazeo move on from The Triumvirate.\nUndoing some of the damage her parents had done was her new calling.
column6: 战后，瓦莱莎投身于慈善事业。\n她帮助马泽奥的人民走出三人执政团的阴影。\n弥补她父母造成的部分伤害，成了她新的使命。

column5: As Pirates, they inflicted wounds upon the culture and people of Mazeo.\nBeing their daughter, she felt qualified to try and make up for what they did.\nAnd so, she would go down in history as one of Mazeo's greatest public figures.
column6: 身为海盗，他们给马泽奥的文化与人民留下了创伤。\n作为他们的女儿，她觉得自己有责任尽力弥补他们所做的一切。\n于是，她作为马泽奥最伟大的公众人物之一载入史册。

column5: She didn't ignore Valinorth, however, and still paid frequent visits.\nTrusting Fortaime to take care of her home, she did the same for Mazeo.\nTogether, they helped ensure that both nations lived strong, and in harmony.
column6: 不过，她并没有忽视瓦利诺斯，依然频繁回去。\n她信任福泰姆照看她的家乡，自己则为马泽奥做同样的事。\n他们携手让两个国家都强盛而和睦地延续下去。

column5: Though the distance between you and Valessa was great, your love never faded.\nFrequent visits to her new home in Mazeo kept things alive as time passed by.\nFor when love is strong enough, nothing can stand in the face of that passion.
column6: 尽管你和瓦莱莎相隔遥远，你们的爱却从未褪色。\n随着时光流逝，频繁前往她在马泽奥的新家探访，让这份感情始终鲜活。\n因为当爱足够坚定，任何事物都无法抵挡这份热忱。

column5: That is, except for time. However, she passed away surrounded by friends and family.\nHer goal of creating a changed, happy world, was finally accomplished. She was content.\nThe damage done by The Triumvirate, and her parents, was finally undone. There was peace.
column6: 除了时间。然而，她是在亲友的环绕中离世的。\n她创造一个焕然一新、幸福世界的目标终于实现了。她心满意足。\n三人执政团和她父母造成的伤害终于得以弥补。天下太平。

column5: You maintained a close relationship with Valessa from your throne.\nPaying frequent visits to Mazeo, you ensured that your bond never weakened.\nAiding her efforts to repair a fractured Mazeo, the wounds of The Occupation soon healed.
column6: 你身居王座，仍与瓦莱莎保持着亲密的关系。\n你频繁前往马泽奥探访，让你们的情谊从未淡薄。\n你协助她修复破碎的马泽奥，占领时期留下的创伤很快愈合。

column5: And so too, did any wounds her family inflicted on the innocent nation.\nBy the time she passed away, she had achieved her lifelong goal of reparation.\nHer gifts to society, and the world — far outweighed her parents heinous crimes.
column6: 她家人带给这个无辜国度的创伤，也随之愈合。\n到她离世时，她已实现了毕生弥补的心愿。\n她回馈社会与世界的贡献——远远超过了她父母犯下的滔天罪行。

column5: Each year, she'd place flowers on Sauleberg's Spirit Idol.\nThis was to remember you, and the idol that empowered you.\nYou were never forgotten. Not by her, or by the world you served.
column6: 每年，她都会在索尔伯格的灵像前献上鲜花。\n这是为了缅怀你，以及那尊赋予你力量的灵像。\n你从未被遗忘。无论是她，还是你所守护的这个世界。

column5: For as long as she lived, she did this every year, her love unwavering.\nKnown as a strong woman, this was the only time she shed a tear.\nTales of her dedication to your love would live on after her passing.
column6: 只要她活着，她每年都会这么做，她的爱坚定不移。\n作为以坚强著称的女子，这是她唯一落泪的时刻。\n她对你这份爱的执着，在身后仍被传颂。

column5: Each year, she'd place flowers on Sauleberg's Spirit Idol.\nThis was to remember you, and the idol that empowered you.\nYou were never forgotten. Not by her, or by the world you served.
column6: 每年，她都会在索尔伯格的灵像前献上鲜花。\n这是为了缅怀你，以及那尊赋予你力量的灵像。\n你从未被遗忘。无论是她，还是你所守护的这个世界。

column5: For as long as she lived, she did this every year.\nKnown as a strong woman, this was the only time she shed a tear.\nTales of her dedication to your memory would live on after her passing.
column6: 只要她活着，她每年都会这么做。\n作为以坚强著称的女子，这是她唯一落泪的时刻。\n她对你这份追忆的执着，在身后仍被传颂。

column5: Because of your efforts and choices, Valessa survived.\nWhen the whole world stood against her, she faced it, and prevailed.\nYou gave her a gift of a happy, peaceful life. One not lost to senseless war.
column6: 因为你的努力与抉择，瓦莱莎活了下来。\n当整个世界与她为敌时，她直面一切，并且胜出。\n你给了她一份幸福安宁的生活。一份没有被无谓战争夺走的人生。

column5: Fortaime returned to Valinorth, and took on the role of Elder.\nHe stayed true to his word, and united his nation with the rest of Alestia.\nAt the loss of some culture, Valinorth merged with The Monarchy for good.
column6: 福泰姆回到了瓦利诺斯，担起了长老的职责。\n他信守承诺，将自己的国家与阿莱斯蒂亚其余部分联合起来。\n瓦利诺斯以失去部分文化为代价，彻底与王室合并。

column5: A small price to pay, many would say. Valinorth let go of its dead beliefs.\nNo more Spirit Realm. No more Seers. Valinorth was just like every other nation.\nTrade routes were opened, and Valinorth was no longer closed off to outsiders.
column6: 许多人会说，这代价微不足道。瓦利诺斯抛弃了它陈腐的信仰。\n不再有灵界。不再有先知。瓦利诺斯和其他每个国家一样。\n贸易路线开通了，瓦利诺斯不再对外人封闭。

column5: In a way, his nation became almost an extension of Mazeo.\nUpon his passing, he left behind the world he dreamed of creating.\nA unified Alestia. Each nation resting on another for strength and purpose.
column6: 某种意义上，他的国家几乎成了马泽奥的延伸。\n他离世时，留下了他梦想创造的那个世界。\n一个统一的阿莱斯蒂亚。每个国家都倚靠彼此获得力量与意义。

column5: He never got over the loss of his lover, however.\nThe day of your death became a day of festivities for Valinorth.\nThey celebrated the gift of life that you gave to the rest of Alestia.
column6: 然而，他始终没能走出失去爱人的痛苦。\n你离世的那天，成了瓦利诺斯的节庆之日。\n他们庆祝你赠予阿莱斯蒂亚其余部分的这份生命之礼。

column5: On this day, many flowers would line the streets to your home.\nFortaime always kept good on his word of visiting you every day.\nThough you were no longer there, he never stopped honoring your memory.
column6: 这一天，通往你家的街道两旁会摆满鲜花。\n福泰姆始终信守着每天来看望你的诺言。\n尽管你已不在，他从未停止对你的缅怀。

column5: He never got over the loss of his best friend, however.\nThe day of your death became a day of festivities for Valinorth.\nThey celebrated the gift of life that you gave to the rest of Alestia.
column6: 然而，他始终没能走出失去挚友的痛苦。\n你离世的那天，成了瓦利诺斯的节庆之日。\n他们庆祝你赠予阿莱斯蒂亚其余部分的这份生命之礼。

column5: On this day, many flowers would line the streets to your home.\nFortaime still came over every day, keeping your house in tip-top shape.\nHe says it's what you would've wanted. He never stopped honoring your memory.
column6: 这一天，通往你家的街道两旁会摆满鲜花。\n福泰姆依然每天过来，把你的房子打理得一尘不染。\n他说这是你希望看到的。他从未停止对你的缅怀。

column5: You stayed in close contact with Fortaime during your reign.\nAfter merging with The Monarchy, Valinorth was under your jurisdiction.\nHowever, honoring Fortaime's wishes, you let him direct the nation in his own way.
column6: 你在位期间与福泰姆保持着密切联系。\n与王室合并后，瓦利诺斯归你管辖。\n但你尊重福泰姆的意愿，让他按自己的方式治理这个国家。

column5: Your love never waned, despite the distance between you.\nA small ceremony was held to solidify your bond, and have it last forever.\nFrequent visits ensured that things stayed afloat. This lasted until the end of his days.
column6: 尽管你们相隔两地，你们的爱从未消减。\n一场小小的仪式举行了，以巩固你们的羁绊，让它天长地久。\n频繁的探访让这份感情得以维系。直到他生命的尽头。

column5: But he left behind a legacy of love, and happiness.\nA statue of him was erected in Valinorth, to honor his memory.\nBecause of him — the nation entered a new era of peace and prosperity.
column6: 但他留下了爱与幸福的遗产。\n瓦利诺斯为他立起雕像，以纪念他。\n因为他——这个国家步入了和平与繁荣的新时代。

column5: You stayed in close contact with Fortaime during your reign.\nAfter merging with The Monarchy, Valinorth was under your jurisdiction.\nHowever, honoring Fortaime's wishes, you let him direct the nation in his own way.
column6: 你在位期间与福泰姆保持着密切联系。\n与王室合并后，瓦利诺斯归你管辖。\n但你尊重福泰姆的意愿，让他按自己的方式治理这个国家。

column5: Your friendship never waned, despite the new distance between you.\nYou passed off visits to Valinorth as official Monarch business.\nHowever, all you really wanted was to visit Fortaime once more.
column6: 尽管你们之间有了新的距离，你们的友谊从未消减。\n你把前往瓦利诺斯的探访当作君主的公务。\n其实你真正想要的，不过是再见福泰姆一面。

column5: Fortaime survived the war, despite all odds.\nHis strong love for everything around him kept him afloat.\nWhen all hope was lost, he stood up, and challenged death in the face.
column6: 福泰姆排除万难，活过了那场战争。\n他对周遭一切深切的爱支撑着他。\n当所有希望都已破灭，他挺身而出，当面挑战死亡。

column5: And for that, he was never forgotten.\nLiving a long and full life, he was happy.\nAlestia was forever better because of him.
column6: 正因如此，他从未被遗忘。\n他度过了漫长而充实的一生，幸福快乐。\n因为有了他，阿莱斯蒂亚永远变得更好。

column5: After the war, Pro settled down in Mazeo, and started to write.\nHe wanted to chronicle everything about the major players of the war.\nWorking with any rebel survivors, he pledged that their story would never be lost.
column6: 战后，普洛在马泽奥安顿下来，开始写作。\n他想把这场战争中所有重要人物的故事都记录下来。\n他与幸存的反抗军成员合作，立誓绝不让他们的故事被埋没。

column5: His works would go down in history as the most detailed records of wartime.\nPeople would aspire to write like him — but to this date — none have come close.\nConsidered one of the greatest historians in Alestia, he retired and lived a peaceful life.
column6: 他的著作作为最详尽的战时记录载入史册。\n人们都渴望能像他那样写作——但直到今天——无人能及。\n他被视为阿莱斯蒂亚最伟大的史学家之一，退休后过上了平静的生活。

column5: He knew that his writings could influence the people's perception in a large way.\nTo this end — he constantly wrote you letters — to ensure he had your approval.\nHowever, the real reason he wrote, was to keep the love between you alive.
column6: 他知道自己的文字能在很大程度上影响民众的看法。\n为此——他不断给你写信——以确保得到你的认可。\n然而，他写信的真正原因，是想让你们之间的爱延续下去。

column5: Almost operating as a team, you ensured that only the true history was written down.\nAs the victor, you could've told the people anything — but you were a just and honest ruler.\nA ceremony was held in Mazeo to pledge your love to one another, until the end of your days.
column6: 你们几乎像一支队伍一样运作，确保只有真实的历史被记录下来。\n作为胜利者，你本可以随意告知民众任何事——但你是一位公正诚实的统治者。\n一场仪式在马泽奥举行，你们彼此立誓相爱，直到生命尽头。

column5: He knew that his writings could influence the people's perception in a large way.\nTo this end — he constantly wrote you letters — to ensure he had your approval.\nThese Monarch approved writings were the highest seal of quality to Alestians.
column6: 他知道自己的文字能在很大程度上影响民众的看法。\n为此——他不断给你写信——以确保得到你的认可。\n这些经君主认可的文字，在阿莱斯蒂亚人眼中是最高品质的保证。

column5: Almost operating as a team, you ensured that only the true history was written down.\nAs the victor, you could've told the people anything — but you were a just and honest ruler.\nYou helped Pro achieve his dream of using information for good. He never harmed with it again.
column6: 你们几乎像一支队伍一样运作，确保只有真实的历史被记录下来。\n作为胜利者，你本可以随意告知民众任何事——但你是一位公正诚实的统治者。\n你帮助普洛实现了他用信息行善的梦想。他再未用它伤人。

column5: He wrote about you and your sacrifice in vivid detail; along with your shared love.\nIn his mind, it was more important to write about you as a person instead of a hero.\nLegends should be grounded in reality. At least that's how he chose to write about you.
column6: 他生动细致地写下了你与你的牺牲，还有你们共有的爱。\n在他看来，把你当作一个“人”而非英雄来写，更为重要。\n传奇应当扎根于现实。至少，他选择这样书写你。

column5: But he never forgot about the relationship that formed between the two of you.\nA lover, a fighter, a hero. Alestia would remember you in many ways in the years to come.\nBut most importantly — thanks to Pro's writing — you would be a symbol of hope to all.
column6: 但他从未忘记你们两人之间建立的那段情谊。\n爱人、战士、英雄。在往后的岁月里，阿莱斯蒂亚会以许多方式记住你。\n但最重要的是——多亏普洛的书写——你成了所有人希望的象征。

column5: He wrote about you and your sacrifice in vivid detail.\nIn his mind, the most important asset in the war should be remembered.\nBut true to his methods, he wrote about your day-to-day life as well.
column6: 他生动细致地写下了你与你的牺牲。\n在他看来，这场战争中最重要的人物理应被铭记。\n但他一贯的做法，也让他写下了你日常生活的点滴。

column5: Legends should be grounded in reality. At least, that's what he thought.\nIt was important for people to realize you were a person first, and a hero second.\nThis empowered generations to come with the idea that {i}anybody{/i} could be a hero.
column6: 传奇应当扎根于现实。至少，他是这么认为的。\n让人们明白你首先是一个“人”，其次才是英雄，这很重要。\n这让后世之人明白，{i}任何人{/i}都可以成为英雄。

column5: Pro's identity as the mole within The Rebellion never came to light.\nHowever, even if it did — he had done enough to make up for his actions.\nMany aspired to write like him, but none could achieve such prowess.
column6: 普洛作为反抗军内部间谍的身份从未曝光。\n然而，即便曝光了——他所做的已足以弥补他的过往。\n许多人渴望像他那样写作，却无人能达到如此造诣。

column5: After the war, Ulric did his best to assist the throne and serve The Monarchy.\nThere was lots to take care of, and things were chaotic after the fog of war settled.\nBut he was up to the task, and he did everything in his power to make the world a better place.
column6: 战后，乌尔里克竭尽全力辅佐王座，为王室效力。\n要处理的事情很多，战火平息后一切都混乱不堪。\n但他担得起这份重任，竭尽所能让这个世界变得更好。

column5: Ulric, protesting against your decision in Alarinthia, never visited his home nation again.\nDraycu remained in power, and Ulric set his sights on serving The Monarchy instead.\nBecause everybody remained in peace — this was not seen as a loss of any kind.
column6: 乌尔里克因抗议你在阿拉林西亚的裁决，此后再未踏足故国。\n德雷库依旧掌权，乌尔里克便把目光投向为王室效力。\n因为所有人都安然无恙——这并不被视为任何损失。

column5: Draycu's death threw Alarinthia into a state of disarray.\nThough their ways remain unchanged, Ulric never gave up on his dream.\nPerhaps, if he fought hard enough, he'd find another opportunity to change his home.
column6: 德雷库之死让阿拉林西亚陷入混乱。\n尽管他们的做法依旧未变，乌尔里克从未放弃自己的梦想。\n或许，只要他足够努力，就能找到另一个改变故乡的机会。

column5: After the war, Ulric did his best to assist the throne and serve The Monarchy.\nThere was much to take care of, and things were chaotic after the fog of war settled.\nBut he was up to the task, and he did everything in his power to make the world a better place.
column6: 战后，乌尔里克竭尽全力辅佐王座，为王室效力。\n要处理的事情很多，战火平息后一切都混乱不堪。\n但他担得起这份重任，竭尽所能让这个世界变得更好。

column5: In his spare time, he would visit New Alarinthia and assist Vivien as well.\nHaving achieved his dream of a changed nation, it made sense to help out.\nIt would take a while before every Alarinthian adjusted to this new lifestyle.
column6: 闲暇时，他会前往新阿拉林西亚，协助薇薇安。\n既然改变了国家的梦想已然实现，帮忙也是理所当然。\n要让每一位阿拉林西亚人都适应这种新生活，还需要一些时日。

column5: Having lost Vivien in the war, Ulric stood up and took his place as ruler of Alarinthia.\nBecause he was Vivien's Champion, and survived, he did have a claim of leadership.\nBalancing his new duties in Balteus and Alarinthia, his life was busy, and impactful.
column6: 战争中失去了薇薇安后，乌尔里克挺身而出，接替他成为阿拉林西亚的统治者。\n因为他是薇薇安的斗士，且活了下来，确实有继位的资格。\n他在巴尔泰乌斯与阿拉林西亚的新职责之间奔忙，生活忙碌而卓有影响。

column5: Though Pro was lost during the war, his writing endured, and created a legacy.\nHe had the most detailed records of The Rebellion, and wrote about almost everybody.\nEverything you could possibly want to know, down to the smallest detail, had been written.
column6: 尽管普洛在战争中殒命，他的文字留存了下来，铸就了一份遗产。\n他拥有关于反抗军最详尽的记录，几乎写到了每一个人。\n你可能想知道的一切，哪怕是最细微的细节，都被记录了下来。

column5: His work went down in history as one of the most detailed records of wartime.\nEvery soldier — their likes and dislikes — their daily routines; he had written it all.\nGrieving friends would use these texts to keep the memories of their loved ones alive.
column6: 他的著作作为最详尽的战时记录之一载入史册。\n每个士兵——他们的好恶——他们的日常作息；他全都写了下来。\n悲痛的友人会借这些文字让挚爱之人的记忆延续。

column5: It was reported that a man and woman resembling Pro were seen at his memorial.\nHowever, they disappeared as quickly as they had come — never to be seen again.
column6: 据传，在普洛的追悼会上，有人看见一对男女，容貌与普洛十分相似。\n然而，他们来去匆匆——此后再未现身。

column5: You did your best to keep Pro's memory alive, and had all of his writing copied.\nNo matter how small the details, you wanted his work to live on as long as it could.\nAs you went through it all, you shed a tear. He wrote fondly of the love you two shared.
column6: 你竭尽全力让普洛的记忆延续，把他所有的文字都抄录了一份。\n无论细节多么微小，你都希望他的作品能尽可能长久地流传。\n当你翻阅这一切时，你落下了泪水。他深情地写下了你们两人共有的爱。

column5: You did your best to keep Pro's memory alive, and has all of his writing copied.\nNo matter how small the details, you wanted his work to live on as long as it could.\nAs you read it all, you looked back on fond memories, and saw how far you'd come.
column6: 你竭尽全力让普洛的记忆延续，把他所有的文字都抄录了一份。\n无论细节多么微小，你都希望他的作品能尽可能长久地流传。\n当你读完这一切时，你回想着往昔的美好记忆，看到了自己一路走来的历程。

column5: Though he couldn't enjoy this victory with you, you knew he'd be proud.\nTales of your bond during the war ended up outliving the both of you.\nIt showed how friendship and camaraderie can flourish even in war.
column6: 尽管他无法与你共享这份胜利，你知道他会为你骄傲。\n你们战时情谊的传说，比你们两人都活得更久。\n它证明了友谊与袍泽之情即使在战争中也能绽放。

column5: But the most popular of his writings was about you, his love.\nThe world would remember you for an eternity, and the sacrifice you made.\nYour name became a symbol of hope, giving light to anyone in dark times.
column6: 但他最受欢迎的作品，是关于你——他的爱人。\n世界会永远铭记你，以及你所做的牺牲。\n你的名字成了希望的象征，为身处黑暗之人带来光明。

column5: To Pro, it was important that you were remembered as a person first, and a hero second.\nTo this end, he stayed true to his methods — choosing to write about your day-to-day life.\nThough you were remembered as a hero, people realized at heart, that you were the same.
column6: 对普洛而言，让你首先被当作一个“人”、其次才是英雄来铭记，很重要。\n为此，他一贯坚持自己的方式——选择书写你日常生活的点滴。\n尽管你被当作英雄铭记，人们心底也明白，你其实和他们一样。

column5: But the most popular of his writings, was about you — The Monarch.\nThe world would remember you for an eternity, and the sacrifice you made.\nYour name became a symbol of hope, giving light to anyone in dark times.
column6: 但他最受欢迎的作品，是关于你——君主。\n世界会永远铭记你，以及你所做的牺牲。\n你的名字成了希望的象征，为身处黑暗之人带来光明。

column5: To Pro, it was important that you were remembered as a person first, and a hero second.\nTo this end, he stayed true to his methods — choosing to write about your day-to-day life.\nThough you were remembered as a hero, people realized at heart, that you were the same.
column6: 对普洛而言，让你首先被当作一个“人”、其次才是英雄来铭记，很重要。\n为此，他一贯坚持自己的方式——选择书写你日常生活的点滴。\n尽管你被当作英雄铭记，人们心底也明白，你其实和他们一样。

column5: Pro's identity as the mole within The Rebellion never came to light.\nHowever, even if it did — he had done enough to make up for his actions.\nMany aspired to write like him, but none could achieve such prowess.
column6: 普洛作为反抗军内部间谍的身份从未曝光。\n然而，即便曝光了——他所做的已足以弥补他的过往。\n许多人渴望像他那样写作，却无人能达到如此造诣。

column5: Fortaime chose to settle in Mazeo after the war.\nHelping the nation's people adjust to the new world was his goal.\nHowever, this was to make up for the truth of learning that his parents were Pirates.
column6: 福泰姆选择在战后定居马泽奥。\n帮助这个国家的人民适应新世界，是他的目标。\n而这，是为了弥补他得知自己父母曾是海盗这一真相。

column5: Undoing the damage they had done to the nation was his top priority.\nSoon after that, the wounds of Mazeo were healed. Everybody was safe and happy.\nTales of The Occupation and The Triumvirate's wrath soon faded into history, and legend.
column6: 弥补他们给这个国家造成的伤害，是他的首要之务。\n不久之后，马泽奥的创伤便愈合了。人人都安全而幸福。\n占领时期与三人执政团暴政的传说，很快淡入历史与传说之中。

column5: In his eyes, he had made up for any harm his parents had caused the nation.\nWhen he passed away, he was known as one of Mazeo's greatest public figures.\nWithout his help and direction, many say the nation would've never recovered at all.
column6: 在他眼中，他已弥补了父母给这个国家带来的所有伤害。\n他离世时，被誉为马泽奥最伟大的公众人物之一。\n许多人说，若没有他的帮助与指引，这个国家根本不可能恢复。

column5: However, due to Valessa's death, his work became almost doubled.\nHe couldn't become The Elder in her absence, so he arranged an election.\nIt was only fair that Valinorth be taken in the direction that the people wanted next.
column6: 然而，由于瓦莱莎的离世，他的工作几乎加倍。\n在她缺席的情况下他无法继任长老，于是他安排了一场选举。\n让瓦利诺斯接下来由人民决定方向，才算公平。

column5: During all of this, he kept in close contact with you.\nFrequent visits to the throne ensured that your love never waned.\nA small ceremony was held back in Valinorth to solidify your eternal love.
column6: 在这一切之中，他与你保持着密切联系。\n他频繁前来王座探访，让你们之间的爱从未消减。\n一场小小的仪式在瓦利诺斯举行，以巩固你们永恒的爱。

column5: From your new home in Balteus, you helped Fortaime heal a wounded Mazeo.\nHowever, history would remember {i}his{/i} efforts — as your legacy lay elsewhere.\nYou were considered a team, and tales of your love endured both of your passing.
column6: 从你在巴尔泰乌斯的新家，你协助福泰姆治愈了伤痕累累的马泽奥。\n然而，历史铭记的会是{i}他{/i}的付出——因为你的功业在别处。\n你们被视为一个整体，你们爱情的传说比你们两人都活得更久。

column5: During all of this, he kept in close contact with you.\nFrequent visits to the throne kept your bond alive forever.\nFrom your new home in Balteus, you assisted his efforts in Mazeo.
column6: 在这一切之中，他与你保持着密切联系。\n频繁前来王座探访，让你们的情谊永远鲜活。\n从你在巴尔泰乌斯的新家，你协助他在马泽奥的工作。

column5: Though it was a joint effort, history remembered Fortaime's efforts.\nYou would be remembered for other endeavors, but that was fine.\nHe deserved most of the credit for helping to heal Mazeo's wounds.
column6: 尽管这是共同努力，历史铭记的却是福泰姆的付出。\n你会因其他功业被铭记，但那也无妨。\n在治愈马泽奥创伤一事上，大部分功劳都该归于他。

column5: During all of this, he never forgot your sacrifice.\nThough your time as lovers was short, he never got over the loss.\nHe kept your memory alive by telling stories about you to everyone he could.
column6: 在这一切之中，他从未忘记你的牺牲。\n尽管你们作为爱人的时光短暂，他始终未能走出这份失去。\n他逢人便讲你的故事，让你的记忆得以延续。

column5: He focused on the little things, rather than your grand destiny.\nFor example, how your life as children in Valinorth went on.\nThe tale of your love endured, even after your passing.
column6: 他关注的是那些小事，而非你宏大的命运。\n比如，你们在瓦利诺斯的童年生活是如何度过的。\n你们爱情的传说历久不衰，即便在你离世之后。

column5: During all of this, he never forgot your sacrifice.\nHe considered it a necessity to keep your memory alive.\nAlmost never keeping quiet, he told stories of you for his entire life.
column6: 在这一切之中，他从未忘记你的牺牲。\n他认为让你的记忆延续下去是一种责任。\n他几乎从不沉默，终其一生都在讲述你的故事。

column5: He focused on the little things, rather than your grand destiny.\nFor example, how your life as children in Valinorth went on.\nHe thought it important to pass on the idea of humble beginnings.
column6: 他关注的是那些小事，而非你宏大的命运。\n比如，你们在瓦利诺斯的童年生活是如何度过的。\n他认为把“出身平凡”这一理念传承下去很重要。

column5: It wasn't very long until word of Fortaime's other endeavors came to light.\nHaving been the first person to climb The Grand Tree — he was a legend.\nAnd just like he had wished, it soon became a tradition for climbers to scale the tree.
column6: 没过多久，福泰姆其他事迹的消息便传开了。\n作为第一个攀上巨树的人——他本身就是一段传奇。\n正如他所愿，攀爬巨树很快成了一种传统。

column5: This continued for almost an eternity after his passing.\nClimbers would leave notes for him at the top of the tree, close to the heavens.\nThey thought that maybe, somehow, he could read them. They thanked him for all he had done.
column6: 在他离世之后，这一传统延续了近乎永恒。\n攀登者会在靠近天际的树顶为他留下字条。\n他们想着，或许、不知怎的，他能读到这些字条。他们感谢他所做的一切。

column5: Fortaime survived the war, despite all odds.\nHis strong love for everything around him kept him afloat.\nWhen all hope was lost, he stood up, and challenged death in the face.
column6: 福泰姆排除万难，活过了那场战争。\n他对周遭一切深切的爱支撑着他。\n当所有希望都已破灭，他挺身而出，当面挑战死亡。

column5: And for that, he was never forgotten.\nLiving a long and full life, he was happy.\nAlestia was forever better because of him.
column6: 正因如此，他从未被遗忘。\n他度过了漫长而充实的一生，幸福快乐。\n因为有了他，阿莱斯蒂亚永远变得更好。

column5: Valessa perished during the final assault on Balteus.\nA memorial was erected near Valinorth, and she would never be forgotten.\nHer bravery, sacrifice, and loving nature — empowered many for years to come.
column6: 瓦莱莎在对巴尔泰乌斯的最后进攻中牺牲了。\n瓦利诺斯附近立起了一座纪念碑，她永远不会被遗忘。\n她的勇敢、牺牲与仁爱——激励了此后许多年的人们。

column5: In the wake of her death, a formal election was held for Valinorth's next Elder.\nHowever, to honor her wishes and views, Valinorth remained independent.\nIt stayed this way for as long as time could tell, honoring her sacrifice.
column6: 她去世后，瓦利诺斯为选出下一任长老举行了正式的选举。\n然而，为了尊重她的意愿与主张，瓦利诺斯保持独立。\n在漫长的岁月里，它一直如此，以纪念她的牺牲。

column5: Fortaime, as the Elder of Valinorth, would go on to write about her.\nThese books would eventually be lost to time, and become legends.\nEverybody knew Valessa by name, and aspired to her greatness.
column6: 身为瓦利诺斯长老的福泰姆，后来写下了关于她的文字。\n这些书最终湮没于时光，化为了传说。\n人人都知道瓦莱莎的名字，都向往她的伟大。

column5: Though your time as lovers was short, you never forgot about Valessa.\nReturning to Valinorth each year, you pay your respects by resting flowers at her home.\nFortaime keeps it in immaculate condition, saying it's what she would have wanted.
column6: 尽管你们作为爱人的时光短暂，你从未忘记瓦莱莎。\n每年回到瓦利诺斯，你都在她故居前献上鲜花，以表敬意。\n福泰姆把那里打理得一尘不染，说这是她希望看到的。

column5: You would return to Valinorth once a year, on the eve of her death.\nLaying flowers in front of her home, you pay your respects, and mourn.\nFortaime keeps the house in immaculate condition, saying it's what she'd want.
column6: 你每年都会回瓦利诺斯一次，就在她忌日的前夕。\n在她故居前摆上鲜花，你表达敬意，寄托哀思。\n福泰姆把房子打理得一尘不染，说这是她希望看到的。

column5: Though your time in this world was both short, tales of your love endured.\nOn the anniversary of your deaths, flowers would litter the streets near your homes.\nThis became a tradition, never lost to time — and your exploits were always honored.
column6: 尽管你们在这世上的时光都很短暂，你们爱情的传说却流传了下来。\n在你们离世的周年纪念日，你们故居附近的街道上会撒满鲜花。\n这成了一项传统，从未被时光磨灭——你们的事迹始终被铭记。

column5: Though your time in this world was both short, tales of your bond endured.\nOn the anniversary of your deaths, flowers would litter the streets near your homes.\nThis became a tradition, never lost to time — and your exploits were always honored.
column6: 尽管你们在这世上的时光都很短暂，你们情谊的传说却流传了下来。\n在你们离世的周年纪念日，你们故居附近的街道上会撒满鲜花。\n这成了一项传统，从未被时光磨灭——你们的事迹始终被铭记。

column5: She was gone, but never forgotten.
column6: 她虽已离去，却从未被遗忘。

column5: During your reign, you had never known a more loyal ally.\nThough his past was with The Inquisition, his future was with you.\nYour love was strong, and ruling together was a joy. The world was at peace.
column6: 在你统治期间，你从未有过比他更忠诚的盟友。\n尽管他的过去属于审判庭，他的未来却属于你。\n你们的爱坚定深厚，共同执政是一种喜悦。天下太平。

column5: He took on the job of helping the world adjust to the new status quo.\nSpreading the news of The Triumvirate's fall, he helped people understand.\nIt was a task as monumental as it was long to complete — but he did complete it.
column6: 他承担起了帮助世界适应新秩序的重任。\n他传播三人执政团覆灭的消息，帮助人们理解这一切。\n这项任务既艰巨又漫长——但他确实完成了它。

column5: The world embraced your rule, and Alestia was forever better because of it.\nInsurrections were rare, and insignificant. Things were peaceful, all thanks to you.\nAs your right hand — and lover — Ulric did everything in his power to keep it that way.
column6: 世界接受了你的统治，阿莱斯蒂亚因此永远变得更好。\n叛乱稀少而微不足道。一切安宁，皆因有你。\n作为你的左右手——也是你的爱人——乌尔里克竭尽所能维持这份安宁。

column5: Thanks to your efforts in lifting his curse, Ulric was finally able to grow old.\nThough death was now capable of taking him, he seemed happier than ever before.\nEspecially now that he had somebody like you by his side to grow old with him.
column6: 多亏你努力解除了他的诅咒，乌尔里克终于能够老去了。\n尽管死亡如今能够带走他，他却似乎比以往任何时候都更幸福。\n尤其是现在，有像你这样的人陪伴在侧，与他一同老去。

column5: With Ulric's curse of immortality still in effect, he outlived every survivor.\nHe eventually came to terms with this, and started to enjoy his eternal life.\nAt least now, the world was a beautiful place to live in. He no longer desired death.
column6: 由于乌尔里克的永生诅咒依然存在，他比所有幸存者都活得更久。\n他最终接受了这一点，并开始享受自己永恒的生命。\n至少如今，这个世界已是个美丽的栖身之所。他不再渴求死亡。

column5: During your reign, you had never known a more loyal ally.\nThough his past was with The Inquisition, his future was with The Monarchy.\nYou were seen as the best of friends — and that made working together a joy.
column6: 在你统治期间，你从未有过比他更忠诚的盟友。\n尽管他的过去属于审判庭，他的未来却属于王室。\n你们被视为最好的朋友——这也让共事成为一种喜悦。

column5: It was his job to help the world adjust to your leadership.\nHe spread the news of The Triumvirate's fall, and helped people understand.\nIt was a task as monumental as it was long to complete — but he did complete it.
column6: 帮助世界适应你的领导是他的职责。\n他传播三人执政团覆灭的消息，帮助人们理解这一切。\n这项任务既艰巨又漫长——但他确实完成了它。

column5: The world embraced your rule, and Alestia was forever better because of it.\nInsurrections were rare, and insignificant. The world was at peace, all thanks to you.\nAs your right hand — Ulric did everything in his power to help keep it that way.
column6: 世界接受了你的统治，阿莱斯蒂亚因此永远变得更好。\n叛乱稀少而微不足道。天下太平，皆因有你。\n作为你的左右手——乌尔里克竭尽所能协助维持这份安宁。

column5: Thanks to your efforts in lifting his curse, Ulric was finally able to grow old.\nThough death was now capable of taking him, he seemed happier than ever before.\nPerhaps because he knew he'd leave behind a changed world — happy and peaceful.
column6: 多亏你努力解除了他的诅咒，乌尔里克终于能够老去了。\n尽管死亡如今能够带走他，他却似乎比以往任何时候都更幸福。\n或许是因为他知道，自己将留下一个焕然一新、幸福安宁的世界。

column5: With Ulric's curse of immortality still in effect, he outlived every survivor.\nHe eventually came to terms with this, and started to enjoy his eternal life.\nAt least now, the world was a beautiful place to live in. He no longer desired death.
column6: 由于乌尔里克的永生诅咒依然存在，他比所有幸存者都活得更久。\n他最终接受了这一点，并开始享受自己永恒的生命。\n至少如今，这个世界已是个美丽的栖身之所。他不再渴求死亡。

column5: With your sacrifice, there was nobody left to lead Alestia.\nUlric, stepping up, took on the role of First King of The Monarchy.\nHis goal was clear — to educate the world on the new status quo.
column6: 由于你的牺牲，再没有人来领导阿莱斯蒂亚。\n乌尔里克挺身而出，担起了王室首位国王的角色。\n他的目标很明确——让世界了解新的秩序。

column5: People slowly learned and adjusted to news of The Triumvirate's fall.\nBut with many years of hard work, they had come to enjoy Ulric's rule.\nAlestians lived in peace, never fearing what their rulers may do to them.
column6: 人们慢慢了解并适应了三人执政团覆灭的消息。\n经过多年的努力，他们终于乐于接受乌尔里克的统治。\n阿莱斯蒂亚人安居乐业，从不担心统治者会对自己做什么。

column5: He never forgot the romance that blossomed along your journey.\nEven though you were lost, he still stayed loyal to you and your memories.\nThough people thought he refused to move on — he knew this wasn't true.
column6: 他从未忘记你们旅途中萌生的那段恋情。\n即便你已逝去，他依然忠于你，忠于对你的回忆。\n尽管人们以为他不愿走出来——他知道事实并非如此。

column5: With his curse lifted, he was no longer afraid of dying.\nHe knew that if he did, he might see his love again in the afterlife.\nThis thought is what kept him going when things as a ruler got rough.
column6: 诅咒解除后，他不再畏惧死亡。\n他知道，若自己死去，或许能在来世与爱人重逢。\n正是这个念头，支撑他度过身为统治者时的艰难时刻。

column5: He served Alestia for an eternity because of the curse of immortality upon him.\nOver time, he became known as The Immortal King of Alestia. An interesting title.\nThe people didn't complain about this, however. He was seen as a great ruler.
